articles.title_orig: Apple iPhone Duo preorders sell out, deliveries extend to late January
articles.title_zh: Apple iPhone Duo preorders sell out, deliveries extend to late January
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Preorders for Apple's ( AAPL ) $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo sold out in minutes after opening Friday, with delivery dates jumping from Oct. 23 to late January.
Apple's most ambitious iPhone yet, the passport-sized Duo features a 5.4-inch front display and a 7.6-inch foldable inner screen, with a nano-texture finish that helps prevent glare while making the panel's center crease all but invisible.
The book-style foldable is a first for Apple, which has sat out of the folding-phone market for years, leaving rivals Samsung ( 005930.KS ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) to grab market share and iterate on their designs.
But Apple is notorious for letting other companies do the legwork to develop a new market, only to swoop in and grab its own piece of the pie. That's exactly what the iPhone maker did with the AirPods and Apple Watch, which have become bestselling devices in their respective categories.
The iPhone Duo brings a number of new features to Apple's all-important product line, including the ability to run two apps side by side or two windows of the same app simultaneously.
Apps seamlessly transition from the front screen to the main display and back. You can also take advantage of the Duo's foldable design by positioning it like an open laptop on your desk and viewing content on the top of the screen while navigating on the bottom half.
In standing mode, you can position the Duo like a tent on a flat surface to watch shows and movies or use the phone as a high-powered clock for your nightstand.
Apple has also thrown in some extras on the camera. When you unfold the phone and open the camera app, the front screen will provide your subject with a preview of your shot. The idea is to spare friends, couples, and everyone in between the awful experience of having someone take your picture, only to immediately look at the result and demand a redo.
The Duo gets ultrawide-angle and wide-angle rear cameras, but no telephoto option. Up front, the phone gets Apple's Center Stage camera, which helps keep the user in view even if they move side to side.
There's also a FaceTime camera hidden beneath the main folding screen.
Foldable phones are still a relatively niche market segment. According to market research firm IDC , manufacturers were projected to ship 1.25 billion units in 2025. Foldables were expected to make up just 20.6 million of those.
But the company said it anticipates foldable smartphones will account for roughly 10% of the market by 2029. It hit a major cumulative milestone in 2026 with total lifetime units set to surpass 100 million by the end of the year, according to Counterpoint Research's latest Foldable Smartphone Market Forecast .

articles.title_orig: Why CoreWeave, Nebius, and other neocloud stocks are being pounded: Goldman Sachs explains
articles.title_zh: Why CoreWeave, Nebius, and other neocloud stocks are being pounded: Goldman Sachs explains
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Neocloud stocks like CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ) are poised to cap off a horrible week in their relatively short time in public markets.
CoreWeave and Nebius stocks are both down about 15% just in the past five days.
While concerns about CoreWeave's financial health are being blamed for the neocloud stock routs, the reality is that it's not just a CoreWeave issue. The overall financial health of the AI economic system build-out is being more closely scrutinized in a land of higher-for-longer interest rates.
Goldman Sachs explained the pressure quite well in a new note on Friday.
US dollar high-yield AI-related debt spreads widened by 25 basis points between Oct. 13 and 14, reaching a new high of 360 basis points over Treasurys. By contrast, non-AI-related debt spreads were only two basis points wider and remain below their March peak, Goldman Sachs pointed out (see charts below).
Within AI-related debt issuers, the widening has been concentrated in AI-related corporate bonds and data center project finance.
"While some softer AI-related sentiment can move datacenter bonds wider, especially if there is a reassessment around off-taker credit risk, we view AI-related corporate bonds, from either neoclouds or firms with significant frontier lab exposure, as being at the epicenter of the funding cost debate," Goldman Sachs strategist Amanda Lynam explained. "Further removed AI-adjacent Energy and Utilities have been more resilient, in our view partly reflecting more diversified revenue streams and a relatively defensive earnings profile. We think the widening reflects a reassessment of the economics of the AI buildout, particularly for lower-rated borrowers that are more exposed to higher-for-longer rates and potential energy-cost pressures."
Lynam sees "some near-term reversal" of the recent sell-off in US high-yield debt tied to AI. But she acknowledges that "dispersion across AI-related issuers is likely to remain high."

articles.title_orig: Neurocrine Biosciences Presents Real-World Evidence Mapping the Lifelong, Evolving Impact of Classic Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia
articles.title_zh: Neurocrine Biosciences Presents Real-World Evidence Mapping the Lifelong, Evolving Impact of Classic Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia
articles.content_orig:
SAN DIEGO , Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: NBIX ) today announced new real-world data demonstrating how the clinical and day-to-day impact of classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia can vary among individuals and evolve throughout a patient's life. The findings will be presented at the Endocrine Nurses Society Annual Symposium 2026, taking place Oct. 16-17 in Phoenix.
The analysis used a novel patient journey mapping approach to combine de-identified electronic medical records from CAHtalog ® , a registry of patients with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) in the United States developed by Neurocrine in partnership with the CARES Foundation . CAHtalog was designed to characterize treatment patterns over time, natural history, and impact of CAH. The records used for this analysis spanned decades of care across providers, specialties, and health systems, allowing clinical, treatment, monitoring, and humanistic experiences to be examined within individual patients with CAH.
"Classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia is a complex, lifelong disease, and every person living with CAH experiences the condition differently, with needs that change over time," said Eiry W. Roberts, M.D., Chief Medical Officer, Neurocrine Biosciences. "By connecting decades of real-world medical records into longitudinal patient journeys, this analysis reveals how the impact of the condition accumulates across the lifespan and highlights challenges that might otherwise be missed in traditional clinical assessments. These insights may help healthcare professionals anticipate periods when patients could benefit from additional education, support, and coordination from their care team."
Electronic medical records from 10 adults (four males, six females) with classic CAH in the CAHtalog registry were used to construct aggregated and sex-stratified patient journeys. * The data comprised more than 2,800 CAH-relevant events representing more than 300 patient-years of medical history. Patient journeys were developed using large language model-assisted analysis and were reviewed and validated by the study team.
Patient records reflected a range of clinical and day-to-day challenges across life stages. Impacts emerged in infancy and centered on diagnosis, treatment, managing acute illness, and preparing caregivers for emergency steroid use. In childhood, records reflected growth-related concerns with bone-age monitoring becoming increasingly important. During adolescence, puberty brought new androgen-related symptoms and challenges with staying on treatment, while monitoring hormone and steroid levels became a greater focus. In young adulthood, new reproductive, surgical, and transition-of-care needs emerged. In adulthood, patients experienced a wider range of health concerns and greater need for imaging and testing.
Treatment, monitoring, caregiver support, and self-management demands recurred and evolved across life stages. Glucocorticoid dose adjustments and stress dosing, or temporarily increasing steroids during illness, injury, or other periods of physical stress, were documented over time in all 10 patients. Records also reflected ongoing monitoring and care coordination, including specialty referrals, changes in providers, treatment access, and the transition to adult endocrinology. Treatment management evolved from caregiver-led support to increasing self-management. These findings underscore ongoing education and preparedness needs for patients and caregivers.
Routine clinical records captured substantial challenges beyond medical complications, extending to school, work, and daily functioning. These impacts evolved over time from challenges managing treatment and progressing in sports during childhood to disruptions in education, work, and physical activity later in life.
While many treatment and weight-related impacts were shared across sexes, the analysis also identified certain sex-specific aspects of care. Menstrual concerns were documented among females, and testicular imaging and testicular adrenal rest tumor concerns were documented among males.
"Nurses are uniquely positioned to understand the full experience of living with adrenal insufficiency — not only the laboratory values and clinical data, but how the condition affects patients and families as they navigate daily life, transitions in care, and changing needs over time," said Louise Fleming, Ph.D., MSN-Ed, RN, FAAN, presenting author and Professor of Nursing at the University of Virginia School of Nursing. "Recognizing the broader patient journey can help us anticipate when additional education, stress-dosing preparation, self-management support or care coordination may be needed. It also allows us to move beyond responding to individual clinical encounters toward providing more proactive, coordinated and patient-centered care across the lifespan."
* This descriptive analysis was intended to provide qualitative insights into patient experiences rather than quantitative estimates, with some observations based on one or two individuals. The findings are illustrative and should not be interpreted as prevalence estimates or evidence of causality.
Additional Presentations at the Endocrine Nurses Society Annual Symposium 2026 Include:
About Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) is a rare genetic condition that results in an enzyme deficiency that alters the production of adrenal steroid hormones, such as cortisol, aldosterone and adrenal androgens. Severe enzyme deficiency leads to an inability of the adrenal glands to produce enough cortisol and, in approximately 75% of cases, aldosterone. Because individuals with CAH are typically still able to produce androgens, the unused precursors that would normally be used to make cortisol instead result in the production of excess amounts of androgens. If left untreated, CAH can result in adrenal crisis and even death.
Exogenous glucocorticoids (GCs) are necessary to correct the endogenous cortisol deficiency, but historically, doses higher than those needed for cortisol replacement (supraphysiologic) have been used to lower the elevated levels of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and adrenal androgens. However, GC treatment at supraphysiologic doses has been associated with serious and significant complications of steroid excess, including metabolic issues such as weight gain and diabetes, cardiovascular disease and osteoporosis. Additionally, long-term treatment with supraphysiologic GCs may have psychological and cognitive impacts, such as changes in mood and memory. Adrenal androgen excess has been associated with abnormal bone growth and development in pediatric patients, female health problems such as excess facial hair growth and menstrual irregularities, in addition to cardiometabolic and fertility issues in both sexes. The symptoms of high ACTH may include testicular adrenal rest tumors (TARTs).
About the CAHtalog ® Registry In 2021, the CARES Foundation, Neurocrine Biosciences and PicnicHealth partnered to establish the CAHtalog ( C ongenital A drenal H yperplasia: Patien t and Clinic al O utcomes in Real-World Practice Settin g s) Registry. The CAHtalog Registry is a U.S.-based CAH patient registry, or collection of clinical patient data, for patients with CAH due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. The database was developed to support patient-centered clinical research to enhance the scientific community's foundational knowledge about CAH, and ultimately help patients who live with the condition. Patients consent to the inclusion of their data in the registry with CAH researchers primarily utilizing de-identified data. For more information about the CAHtalog Registry, please visit CAHtalog.com .

articles.title_orig: Sexual violence concepts launched online are spilling into the real world – harming women and young men and overwhelming counselors
articles.title_zh: Sexual violence concepts launched online are spilling into the real world – harming women and young men and overwhelming counselors
articles.content_orig:
Andrew Tate, a self-described misogynist and an online influencer with millions of followers, faces charges in several countries of allegedly causing physical harm, including rape and sex-trafficking women and girls.
Tate is a prominent figure in the manosphere , a loosely connected network of online forums and sites united by beliefs in male supremacy. This messaging has increasingly moved to mainstream platforms, as social media algorithms on sites like YouTube and TikTok steer young men and boys toward manosphere content sometimes within minutes of opening an account.
Tate’s behaviors are an extreme example of manosphere ideologies spilling into the physical world, harming women as well as the men and boys taken in by the messaging.
The growth of the manosphere has been attributed to backlash toward the #MeToo Movement , which encouraged women to speak up about sexual violence. There is also evidence that increased isolation and time spent online during the COVID-19 pandemic contributed to many men finding these communities.
Nearly half of U.S. women experience unwanted sexual contact in their lifetimes, and 1 in 5 experience attempted rape or rape .
Some countries are taking initiative to curb sexually violent content online. For instance, the U.K. in 2026 implemented several guidelines for social media companies to reduce the spread of misogynistic and sexually violent content to young men and boys . But U.S. federal and state legislation is not keeping up.
As social scientists in social work and psychology , we study the ways sexual violence and masculinities intersect with digital technologies. The growth and cultural salience of manosphere communities have made them increasingly relevant to the work we do.
A violence prevention specialist we talked to in October 2026 said he is struggling to engage men and boys and to keep up with a changing landscape that includes online messaging .
For every Andrew Tate there are many more people launching misinformation and hateful content about women through topics that seem less directly tied to it , like working out, playing video games or just talking. These conversations connect with peoples’ day-to-day lives, which makes it easy to then slip in disparaging comments about women.
People who counsel sexual violence survivors are also struggling with the added burden of online influence, said Kim Foster, a police department senior victim assistance specialist we also interviewed in October. The women Foster works with are often “expecting to be belittled,” she said. “That’s what they’re seeing online.”
Our team of experts reviewed 105 studies on manosphere communities, including research on nine contemporary social media sites: Reddit, Twitter/X, Twitch, Facebook, TikTok, 4chan, Telegram, Instagram and YouTube.
We found that they collectively hosted 89 unique manosphere communities, not counting YouTube channels. Seventy-five of those communities were on Reddit. Our studies also included data from 195 independent websites and blogs.
These communities use discussions of sexual violence to help recruit and indoctrinate new members. They are united by the idea that feminism has gone too far and women’s rights should be rolled back. Male supremacists assert that men are owed sexual access to women and frame themselves as victims when women exercise their right to decline sex or a relationship , or seek to hold men accountable for sexual harm.
This content is not confined to niche communities. A 2024 survey of 16- to 24-year-olds in the U.K. found that 95% were familiar with Tate , and 41% of boys and men had a favorable view of him.
In the context of rising rates of loneliness in the U.S., a shared badge of victimhood helps recruit and engage men into manosphere communities, where they can find belonging and shared purpose as they cultivate antagonism between genders.
Within these communities, men who are accused of sexual violence are lauded as heroes or martyrs for the male supremacist cause.
Men of the manosphere use what researchers call the DARVO strategy : deny, attack and reverse victim and offender – to frame #MeToo and anti-sexual violence activism as a feminist conspiracy targeting men .
“I’d rather be raped than falsely accused,” a Men’s Rights forum user posted in 2018, showing one way that social media users in the manosphere argue that men, not women , are the true victims of sexual violence.
This positions women as a shared enemy for men to blame for loneliness, frustration or anger .
Manosphere members claim that false rape allegations happen all the time and point to skewed statistics and cherry-picked stories. In reality, research consistently reports that a small minority – roughly 5% – of sexual assault allegations investigated by police are proven to be false.
Manosphere communities also judge what forms of sexual violence are worthy of taking seriously.
A common trope: “real victims” stay silent .
Foster sees this affecting her work: “I think we had really hoped that after the #MeToo Movement, people would be more confident coming forward, but I don’t feel like victims expect to be believed and taken seriously,” she told us.
Manosphere communities contain many references to violence and rape . Participants often call these protected speech or innocent jokes .
But for some men, they are a bridge to further harm toward women .
Pick-up artist and seduction communities teach members that “no” rarely actually means “no.” They teach that women deny sex as a game or to avoid being seen as a slut, a concept which they call “last minute resistance.” Users share detailed stories of sexual encounters – referred to as field reports – to give advice or ask about overcoming last-minute resistance. Our research found that these stories often represent clear disclosures of men sexually assaulting women.
The manosphere socializes boys and men into a worldview where entitlement, victimhood and male supremacy are normalized – making it more difficult for them to achieve healthy, consent-based, gender-equitable relationships .
As social media algorithms push more manosphere content , these types of beliefs surface in the real world.
In a case involving a male teacher preying on a female student, for instance, the  investigation found notes on tactics from a pick-up artist forum in the teacher’s possession, Foster said.
Australian researchers found in 2026 that 40% of teenage boys say they think women lie about domestic violence or sexual assault.
The U.K.’s Online Safety Act calls algorithms that promote or normalize hatred and sexual violence against women an online safety problem . 
The act advises tech companies to remove creator payments for misogynistic posts and diversify algorithmic content types to lessen the impact of digital echo chambers .
But U.S. federal policy on social media does not call out the algorithmic spread of misogynistic content as a concern.
The proposed Kids Online Safety Act calls for online platforms to prevent and mitigate harmful material, such as physical violence or sexual exploitation of children, but does not mention women .
State legislation proposed in California in 2026 would have fined large social media companies for algorithms spreading hate speech or violent content, including promotion of violence against women . But the bill was vetoed by Gov. Gavin Newsom .
New York’s Stop Hiding Hate Act , enacted in 2025, requires large social media companies to report their content moderation policies and how they respond to hate speech. But the law doesn’t address algorithm transparency or gender-related hate speech.
Negative societal beliefs about sexual assault victims have long contributed to low rates of reporting, prosecution and jail time for perpetrators. About 1 in 3 survivors report sexual assault to law enforcement. Meanwhile, a low percentage – just a few percent – of perpetrators serve any prison time .

articles.title_orig: Trump says Ukraine resuming strikes on Russian oil sites is a ‘disgrace’
articles.title_zh: Trump says Ukraine resuming strikes on Russian oil sites is a ‘disgrace’
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: Amber Guyger, ex-Dallas police officer convicted of murder, is released on parole
President Donald Trump has labeled Ukraine’s resumption of strikes on Russian oil refineries a “disgrace,” the latest salvo in his campaign to pressure the U.S. ally over rising gas prices that could cost Republicans in next month’s midterm elections .
Kyiv said Thursday that it would no longer abide by Trump’s “energy ceasefire,” citing Russia’s refusal to halt its own attacks on Ukraine’s power grid. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy angrily accused the U.S. of costing civilian lives by striking deals with Moscow and withdrawing support that is crucial to Kyiv’s defense against the invasion launched by President Vladimir Putin.
Ukrainian officials had raised alarm after gaps in intelligence sharing left Kyiv vulnerable to Russian attacks and restrictions on the Starlink satellite service disrupted military operations.  Zelenskyy said Friday that the technology was still not fully restored.
With Ukraine defying his demands to halt strikes, Trump responded late Thursday.
“If you tell me that Zelenskyy is again shooting at refineries, all he’s doing is making the world oil price higher,” Trump told Newsmax’s Rob Finnerty. “I think that’s a disgrace. There’s plenty of other targets; they don’t have to hit,” Trump said.
“Zelenskyy is not a good guy for us to deal with” on the war, he said, adding that “I think they actually both would like to see it end, but I think I find Zelenskyy to be more difficult to deal with than Putin.”
As his clash escalated with Trump, Zelenskyy was in Brussels on Friday to shore up support from European allies, whom he called “real leaders” as they gathered for a crucial summit.
Ukraine hit a Russian oil refinery Thursday after Zelenskyy said he was “done” with the truce, which Trump had announced to the apparent surprise of both sides in the war. Neither Moscow nor Kyiv reported any new strikes on Russian refineries Friday.
Trump has sought to blame Ukraine’s strikes for destabilizing the price of diesel globally, despite the impact of his own war with Iran .
But this campaign of attacks deep inside enemy territory has given Ukraine crucial leverage, sparking a major fuel crisis inside Russia .
Kyiv hoped this would give it a stronger hand at the negotiating table, but as Washington pushes for an end to the conflict it has taken a series of steps that have caused surprise and alarm among Ukraine and its backers in Europe.
Last week, Trump announced a deal to buy diesel from Russia, an apparent attempt to relieve pressure at the pump for American consumers ahead of the midterm elections but which reversed years of U.S. policy. Trump then called for Kyiv to stop all strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and said Zelenskyy had to be replaced as Ukraine’s leader.
It comes amid mounting questions about whether the U.S. is still sharing critical military intelligence with Ukraine after a pair of major strikes earlier this week that Kyiv said came without a usual advance warning from its partners.
Ukraine also reported a slowing down of the Starlink satellite terminals , which are critical for its army’s communications, drone missions and aerial defenses.
Kyiv said that Starshield, the military version of the technology that is used by Ukraine’s troops, had been limited without any warning.
SpaceX chief Elon Musk, the billionaire Trump ally, said that such decisions were up to the U.S. military and ultimately Trump.
After repeated requests for comment about Musk’s statement, a senior U.S. official told NBC News that “no such request was ever made by the president.” Trump has also denied restricting military intelligence for Ukraine.
Kyiv said Thursday the Starshield service was being restored, but the episode only added to the mounting suspicion in Ukraine that the U.S. was willing to cut it off from battlefield support in order to exert pressure for a peace deal. Asked about the service on Friday, Zelenskyy said that issues were ongoing. “Has the speed been fully restored to what it was? No. Is the speed returning? Yes,” he told reporters in Brussels.
European and Ukrainian officials told NBC News they believed that the moves, coming only days after Trump eased sanctions on Russia’s diesel exports and railed against Zelenskyy, were most likely aimed at pressuring Kyiv into making concessions at the negotiating table amid the stalemate in peace talks.
The Kremlin agreed with Trump on Friday, with spokesman Dmitry Peskov saying it was clear that “Zelenskyy doesn’t want to take responsibility and move toward a peaceful resolution.”
Russia has always stated it’s open to a peace settlement but only on its own hard-line terms, which would see Ukraine ceding significant territory.
Yuliya Talmazan is a reporter for NBC News Digital, based in London.

articles.title_orig: New Guidelines Strongly Support Hormone Therapy for Common Menopause Symptoms
articles.title_zh: New Guidelines Strongly Support Hormone Therapy for Common Menopause Symptoms
articles.content_orig:
ACOG issued its most comprehensive menopause guidance, grading treatments for VMS, sleep, and mood symptoms.
The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) has issued its most comprehensive guidance to date on managing menopause, with a new clinical practice guideline covering menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), nonhormonal medications, and nonpharmacologic treatment of vasomotor symptoms (VMS), sleep disturbance, and mood symptoms. Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13, published online October 15, 2026, in Obstetrics & Gynecology , replaces Practice Bulletin No. 141 from January 2014. 1,2
According to the guidance, 50% to 92% of women in menopause report VMS, 16% to 66% of women in the United States report menopause-related sleep disruption, and more than one-third of perimenopausal and postmenopausal women worldwide report depressive symptoms. ACOG is also developing companion guidance on genitourinary syndrome of menopause, expected in 2027. 1
ACOG used a modified GRADE framework to build its recommendations from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and each one carries 2 ratings:
Evidence quality ranges from high (RCTs and meta-analyses without serious flaws, unlikely to change with further research) to moderate (RCTs with some limitations), low (RCTs with serious flaws or limited observational data), and very low (unsystematic clinical observations). Ungraded good practice points reflect expert opinion where evidence is extremely limited or absent.
Below, see recommendations and associated recommended strength along with quality of evidence, quoted from the clinical practice update published in Obstetrics & Gynecology . 2
In a meta-analysis cited by the guideline, estrogen therapy with or without a progestogen reduced VMS frequency (relative risk [RR], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.33-0.57) and severity (RR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.17-0.50) vs placebo or no treatment. A network meta-analysis of 32 RCTs ranked transdermal estradiol plus a progestogen as the most effective option for reducing VMS frequency.
For sleep, a meta-analysis of 15 RCTs (N = 27,715) linked MHT with improved self-reported sleep quality (standardized mean difference [SMD], −0.13; 95% CI, −0.18 to −0.08), but not with objective polysomnography measures. Transdermal and 17β-estradiol regimens showed the largest effects.
In this tissue-selective estrogen complex, bazedoxifene replaces the progestogen to limit endometrial and breast stimulation, which the guideline notes may suit patients who want to avoid progestogen-related bleeding and breast tenderness. In a post hoc SMART-2 analysis, participants reached a 50% reduction in hot flush frequency within 8 to 10 days. Pooled safety data showed no increase in breast cancer, endometrial cancer, venous thromboembolism (VTE), stroke, or coronary heart disease (CHD) vs placebo, although follow-up extends only to 2 years.
Regarding the use of the phrase “hot flush,” ACOG noted in the guidance that, “Although the sudden sensation of extreme heat in the upper body, particularly the face, neck, and chest, is sometimes referred to as a ‘hot flash,’ the term “hot flush” is preferred because it conveys that the sensation is not necessarily momentary and typically lasts 1-5 minutes.”
The timing recommendation draws on a Cochrane review of 19 trials (N = 40,410). Participants who began MHT before age 60 years or within 10 years of menopause onset had a lower risk of CHD (RR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.29-0.96), similar stroke risk, and higher VTE risk (RR, 1.74; 95% CI, 1.11-2.73). Initiation more than 10 years after onset carried greater VTE risk (RR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.37-2.80) and elevated stroke risk (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.06-1.38). The guideline also notes that nearly 67% of Women’s Health Initiative participants were aged 60 years or older, limiting generalizability to younger patients, and that in 2025 the FDA removed boxed warnings for cardiovascular disease, breast cancer, and probable dementia from MHT labeling.²
The guideline adds 3 good practice points on monitoring, discontinuation, and mood:
Paroxetine 7.5 mg/d is the only antidepressant FDA-approved for VMS, but other SSRIs and SNRIs have reduced VMS frequency and severity vs placebo. In a meta-analysis of 7 RCTs (N = 1676), SSRIs and SNRIs moderately improved depression severity (Hedges g, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.32-0.57). The guideline advises generally avoiding fluoxetine and paroxetine in patients taking tamoxifen.
Two agents are FDA-approved: fezolinetant (Veozah; Astellas Pharma US), a neurokinin-3 receptor antagonist, and elinzanetant (Lynkuet; Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals), a dual neurokinin-1 and neurokinin-3 receptor antagonist.
In pooled SKYLIGHT 1 and 2 data, fezolinetant benefits appeared as early as day 1 and were maintained for 52 weeks. Its label carries a boxed warning requiring liver function testing before and during the first 9 months of use.
In OASIS 1 (N = 396), 12 weeks of elinzanetant reduced VMS frequency (least squares mean difference, −3.2; 95% CI, −4.8 to −1.6) and sleep disturbance (least squares mean difference, −5.6; 95% CI, −7.2 to −4.0) vs placebo; its label recommends liver testing at baseline and 3 months.²
“Hormone therapy can be a great option—and in many cases, the best option—but may not be appropriate or helpful for every person experiencing menopausal symptoms,” said Robert P. Kauffman, MD, MSCP, FACOG, coauthor of the guidance.¹
“It was important when creating this guidance to address a variety of treatment options—whether hormonal or nonhormonal, or even nonpharmacologic—to ensure that clinicians have the information they need to help patients manage vasomotor, sleep, and mood symptoms. We have evaluated the data behind a variety of treatment options to ultimately help more women get the care that’s right for them as individuals,” said Kauffman.
Gabapentin reduced VMS frequency in a meta-analysis of 7 RCTs (mean difference, −2.77; 95% CI, −4.29 to −1.24), but pooled severity results did not reach statistical significance. Bedtime dosing is advised because of sedation. The guideline does not recommend clonidine as a primary treatment, and notes that oxybutynin’s adverse effects, including cognitive decline in women older than 65 years, limit its use.²
These approaches can be used alone but are generally recommended alongside hormonal or nonhormonal medications. In a meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (N = 1618), CBT produced small-to-moderate improvements in hot flush frequency (Hedges g, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.21-0.51). MBIs reduced sleep disturbance in a meta-analysis of 13 RCTs (SMD, −0.91; 95% CI, −1.28 to −0.54), and exercise reduced sleep disruption scores across 25 RCTs (SMD, −1.60; 95% CI, −2.03 to −1.18). Confidence in the clinical hypnosis data is limited by the small number of studies and methodologic concerns, while acupuncture trials have shown mixed results vs sham and were conducted mostly in China. Given their low risk, the guideline considers both reasonable as part of a multimodal approach.
The guideline also states that evidence does not support the efficacy or safety of phytoestrogens, such as soy isoflavones, or herbal supplements, which are not regulated by the FDA or tested for safety, efficacy, or purity.²
“Racial, cultural, and socioeconomic factors affect how individuals experience menopause and what level of care they receive. Physicians need to be aware of these disparities and inequities so that we can understand the barriers facing our patients and help to close these gaps in care,” said Catherine D. Cansino, MD, MPH, FACOG, author of the guidance.
ACOG also called for earlier, more comprehensive patient education so that patients can recognize menopause symptoms and seek treatment sooner.¹

articles.title_orig: Nicosia: Inside the world's last divided capital
articles.title_zh: Nicosia: Inside the world's last divided capital
articles.content_orig:
Decades after the Berlin Wall fell, Cyprus's capital remains cleaved in two and separated by watchtowers, barbed wire and a UN buffer zone.
Moments after passing Nicosia's weathered Venetian walls, I followed a series of chain-link fences topped with barbed wire into a no-man's land. Here, at the checkpoint, I was suddenly surrounded by watchtowers and crumbling buildings in the heart of the United Nations buffer zone – a geopolitical scar cutting directly through Cyprus's capital.
A guard inside a pop-up tent eyed our passports before waving us through to the other side. Even though I was in the same city on the same Mediterranean island, I had just left the Republic of Cyprus and the European Union. Now, I was standing in self-declared state of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), in the middle of the world's last divided capital.
In 1974, Turkish forces invaded northern Cyprus in response to a military coup backed by the junta ruling Greece, leading to the displacement of 150,000 Greek Cypriots and 50,000 Turkish Cypriots across the island. Ever since, Cyprus, and its capital of Nicosia, has been cleaved in two, with one side ruled by the island's Greek Cypriot majority, and the other run by its Turkish minority.
Today, visiting this divided Mediterranean city offers travellers a rare glimpse at a place where residents have been separated from their neighbours for more than 50 years.
For the past seven years, I've lived in arguably the world's most famous formerly divided city, Berlin. The scars of the Berlin Wall are a short walk from my home in the former East, and I regularly move across both sides. After learning how the city's decades of division have shaped the place I now call home, I was curious to see the last capital where such a border still remains.
Before the war, Cyprus's only international airport was in the heart of Nicosia, but for the last 52 years, its rusting remains have sat abandoned in the middle of the UN buffer zone (known as the Green Line). So I flew into Paphos, a coastal city in south-west Cyprus, and took a two-hour bus ride to Nicosia, where I signed up for the Walk Talk Cyprus tour led by local Greek Cypriot Eleni Ellinas.
"I started this journey because I felt that Cyprus, and Nicosia in particular, is often oversimplified or misunderstood by outsiders," she said. "People read about the conflict in history books or news headlines, but they rarely get to feel the living, breathing soul of the city or understand what daily life actually looks like along a crossing."
Ellinas was just four years old when years of ethnic and nationalist tensions between Greek and Turkish Cypriots led Turkish forces to invade northern Cyprus. The fighting forced her family out of their home in Famagusta (modern-day Gazimağusa, in the TRNC) and into a refugee camp on the island's south-eastern coast.
"Life in the camp was harsh," she recalled. "My mother, sister, and I were ill. When my father came to check on us and saw the dire conditions we were living in, he knew he had to save his family. He managed to drive us to the RAF base in Akrotiri, and we were fortunate to be evacuated by British forces to the UK."
Their hearts never left Cyprus, so in 1980, the family returned to the island and relocated in Nicosia. "This city welcomed us, embraced our broken pieces and slowly became the place where we laid down new roots and made a home."
In 1983, a separate Turkish Cypriot state was established unilaterally. Yet, it wasn't until 2003 that travellers and Cypriots alike – both Greek and Turkish – were allowed to cross the internationally unrecognised border separating each side. Today, the Republic of Turkey is the only nation to officially recognise the TRNC.
Ellinas says she remembers crossing the border for the first time since fleeing like it was yesterday.
"Stepping across was like walking straight into a dream," she said. "As I walked through those neighbourhoods for the first time as an adult, it felt like I was stepping back into the 1970s… It felt completely surreal, overwhelming and deeply emotional."
In 2019, Ellinas launched her tours "to share the soul of the island I love so dearly" and convey that emotion to travellers.
Ellinas' tours start at the Ledra Palace Checkpoint, the first crossing that Turkish Cypriot authorities opened inside the demilitarised UN Green Line in 2003.
The Ledra Palace was once Cyprus's most famous hotel, a luxury property that opened in 1949 and frequently hosted politicians and actors like Elizabeth Taylor, Richard Burton and Sophia Loren. It also became the site of intense fighting during the 1974 invasion. Bullet holes can still be seen throughout the exterior, walled off today by UN peacekeeping forces with barbed wire. Following the ceasefire, it was used as a headquarters and barracks for UN peacekeepers until 2019.
Today, homes and other buildings caught in the middle of the buffer zone remain abandoned and frozen in time. On the other end of the road near the Ledra Palace, Ellinas pointed out the TRNC border crossing. The word "FOREVER" stands in large, emboldened red letters underneath the name "Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus". Similarly, a giant TRNC flag painted on the hillside north of Nicosia with the message, "How happy is he who says I am a Turk" is visible from the Greek side.
Ellinas expressed disappointment over the nationalistic messaging and expressed hope that the island will one day be reunited.
"While some [Cypriots] remain stuck in the past, there is an overwhelming longing for unity felt by many," she said. "You see this energy bringing new life to areas like the restored streets around Ermou [the city's premier shopping hub up until the war] where art, youth and community are reclaiming space that was once deserted and dead."
To help visitors experience both sides of Nicosia, Ellinas encourages all travellers to cross into the Turkish side following the end of her tour.
"You cannot truly understand a divided capital by looking at it through a single window," she said. "You have to feel both perspectives."
The UK and US don't have any travel warnings to Cyprus. Non-EU citizens need a passport to cross the UN buffer zone in Nicosia, whereas EU citizens can simply present a national ID card or passport. Since the Greek side uses the Euro and the Turkish side uses the Turkish lira, most international travellers choose to stay in the southern Greek Cypriot side.
For her, Cyprus is still in many ways one place. The two sides have a shared history, architecture, and in her words, pain.
"Suffering was experienced by all Cypriots, regardless of background," she said. "When you step across and walk through places like the old Armenian quarter in Arab Ahmet, or stroll down historic Victoria Street, it feels as though time stood frozen in place. Seeing the old homes, breathing in the quiet atmosphere, and connecting the human threads on both sides gives travellers a complete, empathetic picture of what this island truly is."
Passing through the checkpoint in the UN buffer zone and stepping foot into the TRNC felt like entering a different country. Whereas the Green Line along the Greek side was marked by abandoned buildings, the Turkish side appeared much livelier. Pedestrians spilled out onto the narrow streets, the savoury aroma of Turkish kebabs filled the air and a domed mosque from a 16th-Century caravanserai soon appeared before me.
I visited some of the sights that Ellinas had recommended, namely the 16th-Century Büyük Han caravanserai and the Samanbahçe Evler neighbourhood – a one-of-a-kind social housing estate with geometric mud-brick units. The highlight, though, was my stop at the Rüstem Kitabevi , a bookstore founded in 1937 where I sipped coffee and ate carrot cake after admiring towers of hardback tomes spread across two floors.

articles.title_orig: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft’s promises
articles.title_zh: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft’s promises
articles.content_orig:
Over the past week, the laptop Microsoft sent me has been summarizing books and movies, generating images from my imagination, and running a 70-billion-parameter AI model that would be a stretch to fit on most laptops. It also played AAA games at a speed and fidelity I would have thought impossible on an ARM system just a year ago. Microsoft wants to sell you one computer for all of your needs, and for once that doesn’t feel like total marketing fluff. Mostly.
Microsoft is throwing both arms around the new Nvidia RTX Spark platform with the Surface Laptop Ultra—and setting its sights on the would-be MacBook Pro buyer, or as the company called it, “a high performance audience.” The bet is that rather than a gaming desktop for fun and a development laptop for work, buyers will pay more for one machine that does both.
The Surface Laptop Ultra arrives at a strange time in personal computing. Recent industry numbers showed a 20 percent drop in total PC shipments year over year in the third quarter of 2026. That’s not just consumer purchasing either—that’s across the board. Between the RAMpocalypse that has exploded consumer prices and an industry fixated on enterprise money, there hasn’t been much new hardware to excite PC enthusiasts.
Microsoft isn’t the only one debuting an RTX-chipped laptop. Dell’s XPS 16 Creator Edition and Asus’s ProArt series (our own Ryan Whitwam ‘s review should be appearing on the front page soon) are betting on the chipset as well. The question when reviewing the Surface Laptop Ultra isn’t whether it can achieve the things that it claims competently, but whether there’s finally a compelling reason for power users to switch to an ARM system, and whether their daily workloads can still be achieved without hiccups when compared to a more traditional x86 offering, or the biggest competitor within the segment, the MacBook Pro.
With a starting price of $2,599, this is not a budget alternative to Apple silicon. This is bleeding-edge hardware, and you’re going to be paying a premium for it. Depending on your selected processor and memory options, MSRP can reach as high as $5,899 . Prospective buyers should note that the lower-specced 24GB unified memory model ships with Windows 11 Home, while the rest of the fleet arrives with Windows 11 Pro. I received the 64GB model for testing, and I think that would probably be the sweet spot for a lot of users to align cost and performance.
I really have to wonder if 24GB is enough to go around when we know that Windows 11 is memory-hungry on its own. When you have to assign a significant portion of that 24GB of unified memory to VRAM for gaming, does performance suffer? An audience question inside the Surface Laptop Ultra review information session asked about the usefulness of the base model, and didn’t get much back other than a vague “useful for smaller models locally” answer. Microsoft may have a more definitive answer to that question a few months from now when software and drivers catch up with hardware.
So has the Microsoft and Nvidia team-up created the ultimate all-in-one laptop? Or is this the industry once again putting the hardware hype cart before the finished-software horse?
The 15-inch mini-LED display might not be enough to get folks to run to the Ultra on its own, but it’s a compelling reason to add it to the list. The 3270×2180 native resolution looks simply stunning whether you’re watching a 4K video, playing games, or just staring at a desktop spreadsheet. I preferred the Enhanced color profile, but Vivid and sRGB modes looked fantastic as well.
Blacks stayed deep against bright, vivid subjects without any sort of visible blooming. I wish I could say the same for my TV. While I can’t quantify how it stacks side by side with the latest MacBook Pro Retina display, I can say that this is a damn nice screen. Viewing angles are superb, colors are punchy, and the 2,000-nit peak brightness kept things legible even in a room flooded with natural sunlight. My only gripe is that in bright rooms, there is glare to contend with. The glossy glass looks fantastic at lower light levels but can act a bit mirror-like in direct sunlight. It hindered my ability to photograph the screen more than it did my ability to use the computer. Still, if you’re looking for a matte-screen laptop, you might want to keep that in mind.
The keyboard on the Surface Laptop Ultra is exactly what you’d expect on a premium machine like this. It’s excellent, if unremarkable. The keys have a shallow but satisfying press, the spacing makes sense for my hands, and the whole package delivers a very comfortable typing experience. I don’t have a whole bunch of laptops lying around to compare it to, but unsurprisingly, the closest would be my 2020 MacBook Pro. Microsoft knows what market it’s going after here, and I don’t mind them lifting direct inspiration from Apple in this department.
The trackpad is similarly competent. It’s absolutely huge, measuring 5.5 inches long by 3.5 inches tall, with excellent tracking accuracy throughout my testing time. Normally, one of the first things I do when plugging in a laptop to work from is to attach an external mouse, but over days of testing, I never reached for the mouse drawer. Microsoft made a point to emphasize the trackpad’s haptic feedback capabilities in native programs during the review information session. I’m not sure if there are still updates left to come that I haven’t received yet, but I can’t recall a time when I noticed additional mouse haptics had kicked in when I opened MS Office or anything. As it stands, the trackpad isn’t groundbreaking, but it is premium enough to be part of an “ultra” laptop.
Microsoft describes the included magnetic charging connection and port as being “the world’s first built-in magnetic USB-C charging experience.” It’s difficult to get upset about the marketing department doing their jobs, but this claim struck me as more of a technical truth than engineering feat. Apple’s MagSafe charging debuted on the original MacBook Pro all the way back in 2006 . The concept of a breakaway magnetic charger isn’t anything new, but technically Microsoft’s assertion holds water in that it is the first USB-C connector on a laptop with a matching magnetic port, rather than a proprietary connector.
Marketing claims aside, the magnetic connection does work well. The port and charger naturally guide themselves together, as magnets do, and made plugging the laptop in to charge in a dark room hassle-free. Normally I’d be holding the cord in one hand while trying to fumble around in the dark for the phone in my pocket and remember the gesture to quickly turn on the flashlight. Now I just have to get the cable within the vicinity, and the magnets do the rest. Perfect for when all I want to do is plug the PC in and go to bed.
What’s perhaps the larger selling point for magnetic charging is the cable’s ability to break away if yanked from the PC. Nothing will ruin your day faster than watching a new laptop fly off the counter. With the breakaway cable, you’re getting peace of mind that your laptop shouldn’t meet the floor should a startled cat or curious toddler come into contact with the cable. I’ve never had it happen with one of my laptops, but that doesn’t mean accidents don’t occur. I simulated a few ‘accidental disconnects’ with modest force, and the cable disconnected dutifully as it should.
While I won’t say that it’s a must-have, it’s certainly a nice-to-have. And in this package it’s certainly the type of premium accessory you’d expect, but it’s not going to move units on its own—not at these price tiers.
According to Nvidia, the RTX Spark N1X is a Grace CPU fused to a Blackwell GPU. Unlike chipsets like AMD’s Ryzen AI and Intel’s Core Ultra series, the N1X has no dedicated NPU—instead it leans on unified memory and the heavy-duty Blackwell GPU for AI work. articles.title_orig: Under US pressure, World Bank says it will back gas “where appropriate”
articles.title_zh: Under US pressure, World Bank says it will back gas “where appropriate”
articles.content_orig:
The World Bank president said on Friday his organisation will continue to support some gas projects in developing countries alongside renewables, nuclear and hydropower, despite criticism from climate campaigners who say fossil gas is expensive and polluting.
"Homes, mines, factories, farms, and growing cities - what do they need? Reliable, affordable baseload power," Ajay Banga told the bank's annual meeting in Bangkok on Friday. "Our approach is balanced by design - a full mix of renewables, hydro, gas where appropriate, nuclear when it makes sense, transmission, grids, storage - the whole thing."
His comments come in a week during which he faced pressure from the US to finance more gas projects and from climate campaigners to stop funding fossil fuels altogether, part of a tightrope he has walked on the bank's climate policy since Donald Trump’s re-election in 2025.

The World Bank president said on Friday his organisation will continue to support some gas projects in developing countries alongside renewables, nuclear and hydropower, despite criticism from climate campaigners who say fossil gas is expensive and polluting.
"Homes, mines, factories, farms, and growing cities - what do they need? Reliable, affordable baseload power," Ajay Banga told the bank's annual meeting in Bangkok on Friday. "Our approach is balanced by design - a full mix of renewables, hydro, gas where appropriate, nuclear when it makes sense, transmission, grids, storage - the whole thing."
His comments come in a week during which he faced pressure from the US to finance more gas projects and from climate campaigners to stop funding fossil fuels altogether, part of a tightrope he has walked on the bank's climate policy since Donald Trump’s re-election in 2025.
The bank ended its support for coal around ten years ago and last year, for the first time, funded no oil projects. It has ended support for gas exploration but still backs some projects to do with transporting and using gas, such as a $140-million project to help Benin, Côte d’Ivoire and Togo in West Africa to import liquefied natural gas (LNG).
While its overall support for fossil fuels wanes, the bank's support for clean energy has been at historic highs over the last few years, with funding of just under $10 billion a year in 2023, 2024 and 2025 - compared to under $1.5 billion a year for fossil fuels.
On Monday, the head of Pakistan's Indus Consortium, Hussain Jarwar, asked Banga at a civil society townhall meeting why the bank is supporting a "volatile" energy source like LNG, which is pushing economies and consumers into debt "when real renewable energy solutions like solar [are] available and supporting communities and industries for clean, accessible and affordable energy source". Global LNG prices hit record highs earlier this year as the Iran war squeezed supplies.
Banga replied that the bank is working with countries to source "baseload productive power" and that "if Pakistan wants to build an energy system that is more self-reliant by going further on different forms of baseload plus top-up energy, we're more than happy to work with it". "We've got no biases in the system - our job is that electricity and water are human rights," he added.
His answer did not satisfy climate campaigners. Sunil Acharya, just transition lead at Recourse, an NGO that works on sustainable development finance, said in a statement that the bank is moving in the wrong direction and Banga's "framing of wind and solar as a ‘top-up’ to nuclear, hydropower and gas misses the opportunity to transform energy systems".
"Fossil gas is bad economics - it exposes countries to volatile global markets and debt while locking public resources into costly infrastructure," the Nepali campaigner said. "The World Bank must stop reproducing the extractive development model of the fossil fuel era and redirect public finance towards 100% renewable economies that deliver energy for all, protect people and nature, and put people’s priorities before private profit."
On Wednesday, however, Banga was pressured from the other direction. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who skipped the Bangkok meeting, issued a statement praising the bank for "beginning to refocus on its core mission of reducing poverty and raising economic growth" after what he called "years of mission creep".
He said the bank should "formally retire its prohibition on financing" gas and oil exploration and production as it "cannot credibly invoke country ownership while categorically excluding upstream projects before their development merits are even assessed". He argued that supporting gas projects would help extend electricity access in Africa.
The US is a major gas exporter and analysts are warning its gas companies will struggle to sell their product abroad in the coming years, as US LNG production expands while buyers in Europe and Asia move away from gas to cleaner sources of electricity.
In July, under US pressure, the World Bank scrapped its target for 45% of its finance to go to climate projects. But, with support from a broad majority of countries, it renewed its climate change action plan. The compromise "could have been a lot worse", E3G climate policy advisor Danny Scull said at the time.
Other multilateral development banks that have the US as a major shareholder, like the Inter-American Development Bank and Asian Development Bank, are now expected to face pressure to scrap their climate finance targets too.
In June 2025, the World Bank ended its ban on support for nuclear power - a move that was welcomed by the US. In his speech on Friday, Banga said the bank would support nuclear retrofits - the modernisation of existing nuclear power stations - alongside the International Atomic Energy Agency, noting that this was "the first such work in 50 years for the bank".

articles.title_orig: World Food Day: UNICEF warns of climate threat to child nutrition
articles.title_zh: World Food Day: UNICEF warns of climate threat to child nutrition
articles.content_orig:
According to a recent UNICEF report, climate change is projected to result in an additional 28 million children affected by malnutrition and 40 million children experiencing stunted growth worldwide by 2050.
As greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise, global temperatures will increase, bringing profound changes to the climate and affecting all the factors that determine childrenâs nutritional well-being.
The effects could also extend to micronutrient and protein deficiencies, with the number of children affected potentially increasing by hundreds of millions by 2050. These impacts, the report explains, would be felt across all age groups, including school-aged children and adolescents.
Climate change is also expected to drive an increase in childhood obesity far beyond the rise attributable to non-climatic factors. Extreme heat, in fact, can limit physical activity, while changing dietary habits, especially in developing nations, may lead to greater reliance on ultra-processed foods.
UNICEF has also warned that the El Niño phenomenon expected in 2026-2027 could become one of the most intense ever recorded. This recurring climate pattern warms parts of the Pacific Ocean and disrupts weather systems around the world.
For children living in countries affected by conflict and humanitarian crises, such as Afghanistan and Chad, El Niño could pose a direct threat to survival by worsening hunger and malnutrition.
In these already fragile settings, conflict, displacement and limited access to essential services leave children particularly vulnerable to further climate-related shocks.

articles.title_orig: Troy Jackson tells Susan Collins to ‘shut up’ during Maine Senate debate
articles.title_zh: Troy Jackson tells Susan Collins to ‘shut up’ during Maine Senate debate
articles.content_orig:
Maine Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson told Republican Sen. Susan Collins to "shut up" after she tied him to a heckler who interrupted their Thursday debate. (Courtesy: News Center Maine, Portland Press Herald)
Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson clashed over billionaire donors, party loyalty and working-class voters Thursday night as their fourth debate took a notably personal turn.
In the debate's top moments, Jackson needled Collins over whether she had meaningfully pushed back on Republican-led decisions she disagreed with. Collins defended her record and questioned whether Jackson would stand up to his own party when pursuing the best interests of Maine.
COLLINS INSISTS SOCIALIST RIVAL WON'T BEAT HER AS MAINE'S MONEY MACHINE: 'YOU'LL LOSE BIG TIME'
Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, faces off against Troy Jackson, the former Maine Senate president and the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, in their fourth debate appearance together on Thursday evening. (Charly Triballeau / AFP via Getty Images; Charly Triballeau AFP via Getty Images)
When a heckler interrupted the debate and began shouting about data centers and climate change, Collins said the man was "obviously one of Troy's supporters."
"Oh shut up," Jackson shot back. "I don't even know that kid."
Near the beginning of the night, Collins questioned whether Jackson had really kept campaign promises to reject billionaire donors that aligned themselves closely with his and other Democratic campaigns, noting FEC contribution records that seemed to clash with those assurances.
"And as far as the billionaires that I might have on my campaign, that is accurate," Jackson admitted. "But I haven't … "
Jackson paused for a moment as members of the crowd gave an audible reaction to the admission.
MAINE DEM SEN CANDIDATE'S 'WORKING CLASS' CRED SHREDDED BY BOTH PARTIES WHEN INTERNET SEES LATEST 'CRINGEY' AD
"I haven’t made any deals like Senator Collins has with those billionaires," he continued. "I’m going to tax those billionaires when I get to the U.S. Senate."
Jackson did not specify what agreements he was referring to.
WATCH: MAINE'S JACKSON ADMITS HAVING BILLIONAIRE DONORS DESPITE PROMISING TO REJECT THEIR MONEY:
Collins also faced questions about her independence from President Donald Trump. At one point, the moderator asked her to identify an instance when she had defied the president and changed the outcome of a decision.
Collins cited her opposition to the confirmation of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth , who faced scrutiny during his nomination over his qualifications and allegations about his personal conduct.
Sen. Susan Collins directs a question to Troy Jackson during a debate at Husson University in Bangor on Thursday. (Gregory Rec/Portland Press Herald via Getty Images)
"At one point, I had organized people to vote against Secretary Hegseth. As you undoubtedly have read, at the very last minute, one of our Republicans changed his mind. Otherwise, he would have been defeated for that job," Collins said.
Jackson countered that Hegseth was ultimately confirmed despite Collins' opposition.
"Senator Collins likes to have it both ways. I mean, the reality is that 100% of the time when Donald Trump needs her, Susan Collins is going to be there. That has happened time and time again," Jackson said.
FORMER OBAMA ADVISOR TELLS DIVIDED MAINE DEMOCRATS TO 'GET OVER YOUR S---' AND WIN THE RACE
Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate Troy Jackson shakes hands with Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, before their debate at the Gracie Theatre in Bangor, Maine on Oct. 15, 2026. Jackson is looking to unseat the five-term senator in November's midterm election. Americans voting in the Nov. 3 midterm elections will decide who controls Congress for the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency, along with dozens of governorships and thousands of state offices. (Charly Triballeau / AFP via Getty Images)
Meanwhile, Collins pointed to what she described as a "major difference between Troy and me. I vote very independently ... I am the most bipartisan member of the Senate."
And referring to Jackson, Collins said, "We don’t need more people who are going to vote a straight party line."
Jackson defended his own independence by pointing to clashes with Democratic Maine Gov. Janet Mills during his tenure in the state Senate .
"How can I be a rubber stamp with my very own governor — a Democratic governor — vetoing 40 of my bills?" Jackson asked.
Jackson had repeatedly challenged Collins over her voting record in their three prior debates . Collins disputed his characterization of her record, arguing that he had overstated how frequently she sided with Trump.
"You have heard Troy say that I vote with the president 92 or 94% of the time; that takes only a third of the votes. If you look at 90% of the votes, you will find that I vote with him 72% of the time, not 95% of the time," Collins said.
The debate took a personal turn near the end when Jackson, a former logger, questioned whether Collins looked down on him because of his working-class background.
"You know, you said consistently that I don't have the experience. You just said it tonight that I wouldn't be able to do the things that you do. Growing up as a working-class person, I have all kinds of experience," Jackson said.
"And so, I guess, you know, what I'm curious about — is it just me that you look down on, or is it working-class people overall?"
Collins rejected the accusation and pointed to her own working-class roots.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Troy, I do not look down on you or on anyone. I grew up in Caribou. My first job was picking potatoes," Collins said. "I have worked since I was age ten, literally since I was age ten. I have enormous respect for all the people of Maine."
The debate came as Collins and Jackson entered the home stretch of the campaign ahead of Maine's Nov. 3 general election, with control of the U.S. Senate at stake.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk reveals ‘world’s first flying car’ at Tesla event
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk reveals ‘world’s first flying car’ at Tesla event
articles.content_orig:
The Tesla Roadster 2 drove up a curved ramp before using SpaceX rocket thrusters to fly, flip and land
Elon Musk has revealed Tesla’s latest model, which he claims will be the world’s first flying car, using technology from his aerospace company SpaceX to “basically fly like a rocket”.
The billionaire, who hosted a demonstration of the Tesla Roadster 2 at the SpaceX rocket development and testing facility in Texas, said the sports car could go from 0 to 60mph in a record time of less than a second and had thrusters.
A video of the event shows the Roadster, which he said was controlled remotely “to make sure we don’t kill anyone”, driving up a curved ramp using suction to grip upside down, before using thrusters to flip, fly and land .
Later in the demonstration the Roadster is seen using the jets to leap over a line of Tesla’s existing models and then accelerate to 60mph in record time.
“Turns out the future does have flying cars,” Musk said in a post on his social media site, X, accompanying a video from the event.
Speaking at the event on Thursday, Musk said: “Flying cars are real. It’s got altitude controls, thrusters and main thrusters in the rear. So it can basically fly like a rocket, it can do rolls, crazy gymnastics.”
“I’m not sure it’s necessarily legal in all jurisdictions,” Musk said, adding that the prototype was “not necessarily a safety optimised car but it takes the fun meter to 11”.
In 2014 Musk expressed his scepticism about a future with flying vehicles .
However, three years later he announced the development of the Roadster 2, which will go into production in 2028 and priced in excess of $200,000, (£150,000), to create an electric sports car “to give a hardcore smackdown to gasoline cars”.
after newsletter promotion
After the event, a Tesla reservation website for expressing interest in the two-seater Roadster 2 showed that a “performance” version of the vehicle would require a £50,000 deposit. A “thrust” version would require a $250,000 deposit.
Meanwhile, a one-seater “rocket” variant with “full flight system” was labelled as being available only by invitation. The car company added that flying it was not permitted on public roads.

Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico criticized Republican opponent Ken Paxton during a Thursday night campaign rally in San Marcos, accusing the state attorney general of avoiding a debate with him ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

"Because if you're applying for the job of U.S. senator, if you're applying for the job of representing 31 million Texans, you should show up to the job interview," he said.

The DOJ filed a complaint against California alleging the suspected noncitizens registered to vote or voted in a federal election. Officials said HSI and federal partners used multiple methods to verify their immigration status.
First assistant U.S. attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California said election officials were given an opportunity to remove noncitizens from their voter rolls and to sequester ballots returned from suspected ineligible voters, but “they refused.”
“We are taking California to federal court to demand that the votes of American citizens not be diluted by noncitizens,” Essayli said.
If found responsible in a court of law, Attorney General Todd Blanche said California “will have seriously undermined confidence in our electoral system and violated laws that protect our nation’s representative system of government.”

"Lindsey passed away very suddenly and unexpectedly, and everybody was devastated, especially Darline and myself," Trump said.
During the campaign call, Trump recalled the late senator's admiration for Darline, describing the respect Lindsey had for her and their close relationship.
The president also praised Darline's work on behalf of South Carolina, describing her as a respected figure who is delivering results for the state.
Trump's remarks came as Republicans seek to maintain control of the Senate in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

The debate comes less than three weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, as Collins seeks another term in the U.S. Senate.
The Maine Senate race is among the closely watched contests as Republicans fight to maintain control of the chamber.

Vance criticized Lawrence, who is running in Michigan's 7th Congressional District, over statements he attributed to the Democrat about the nuclear family, American culture and open migration.

articles.title_orig: Indian police again detain ‘cockroach’ movement founder ahead of protest
articles.title_zh: Indian police again detain ‘cockroach’ movement founder ahead of protest
articles.content_orig:
Police detained India’s “ cockroach ” movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and some supporters on Friday, ahead of a protest called by him in capital Delhi’s central business district, the latest rally to demand the resignation of India’s election chief.
The youth-led “Cockroach Janta Party” (CJP), opposition groups, and student organizations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Dipke called Friday’s protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban.
India’s ‘Cockroach’ movement founder and leaders released from detention after Delhi protest crackdown
The group and left-wing student organisations had urged supporters to gather at the Central Park in New Delhi’s busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag.
The live video on CJP’s Instagram handle showed Dipke coming out of a house and walking towards the street, where police officers stopped him and, after a brief argument, hauled him into a police car and drove away.
“We are detaining you right now,” a police officer could be heard telling Dipke.
“I have not broken any law right now…how can you detain me,” Dipke asked the police officers as he was taken away.
There was no immediate comment from the police on the detention.
“Abhijeet is detained by Delhi Police,” CJP posted on X. “This government is so scared of the youth waving national flag.”
Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, was also detained as she tried to reach Connaught Place with dozens of supporters, local media reported.
Earlier on Friday, police met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Security was stepped up and the park itself shut by civic authorities.
Senior police officer Sachin Sharma told news agency ANI that Dipke was served a notice that asked him to obey the law, and that he was informed of the implications of any violations.
Television images showed dozens of people arriving at Connaught Place amid heavy security, some of them waving small versions of the national flag.
Small protests were also held in financial capital Mumbai and tech hub Bengaluru, while student organizations held a demonstration in the eastern city of Patna, with people waving flags of their organizations and pushing against police barricades.
The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power.
A weeks-long sit-in by its supporters earlier this year forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over exam paper leaks.
The latest demonstrations erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar’s two deputies raised concerns internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems.
The 130 million names that were removed from voter lists starting last year — equivalent to more than the population of Japan — included 28 million people who had died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced, according to the Election Commission.
A weeks-old Gen-Z protest group managed to get India’s Modi to blink. What’s next?
Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslims and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, allegations the commission and the BJP reject.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said the demonstrations were the main opposition Congress party’s attempt to “seize power”.
“Instead of channeling the energy of the youth toward nation-building, they are being used as pawns in the politics of anarchy,” he said at a media briefing on Friday.
This story has been updated with additional developments.

articles.title_orig: La Via Campesina Organizations March on IMF-World Bank Venue, Demanding Food Sovereignty
articles.title_zh: La Via Campesina Organizations March on IMF-World Bank Venue, Demanding Food Sovereignty
articles.content_orig:
Article originally published by The Nation Thailand
The Assembly of the Poor marched towards Bangkok’s Queen Sirikit National Convention Center on October 16, 2026, intending to present six demands to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank, including debt cancellation and greater public oversight of economic policy. The march took place as Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul attended the formal opening of the institutions’ 2026 Annual Meetings, with police maintaining tight security around the venue.
About 500 people gathered at Gate 1 of Lumphini Park in Pathum Wan district for discussions and a rally led by Assembly of the Poor leader Baramee Chaiyarat. Participants included workers, the urban poor and other members of the public.
The gathering marked the International Day of Action for Food Sovereignty and against Transnational Corporations. Organisers called for an end to debt traps and the reclamation of financial and food sovereignty.
Organisers divided participants into groups wearing green, orange, red and black scarves before setting off. Their route followed Sukhumvit Road before turning right at Asok intersection towards the convention centre.
Participants formed columns four abreast. The groups listed included Pak Mun, Hua Na, Kaeng Suea Ten, Rasi Salai–Liang Pha, coconut growers and a group called Kor Lor Por.
Other participating groups included Thung Yao, Tha Khoei, Phu Pha Lek, Tha Dan Dam, Khok Nong Lek, Sirindhorn Dam, a farmers’ debt network, Rasi Salai–Tha Pradit and Nakhon Sawan.
The protesters’ six demands to the IMF and World Bank were to:
About 300 protesters from the People’s Network Against the World Bank and IMF, together with the Non-Governmental Organisation Coordinating Committee on Development, had been camped on Ratchadaphisek Road at Rama IV intersection since October 15.
Leaders identified in the report included Chamnong Nupan of the People’s Movement for a Just Society (P-Move), Sohabudin Lohyapha and Nakita Koetnak. Most participants at the overnight protest were resting or attending to personal needs during the morning.
Crowd-control officers and other police guarded all access routes to the convention centre as Anutin attended the opening ceremony.
The convention centre and surrounding area had been designated off-limits to demonstrations under the Public Assembly Act. The report assessed that the restrictions and security arrangements made it highly unlikely that protesters could hand their demands directly to the prime minister.
