articles.title_orig: Seven sailors missing after drones strike tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast
articles.title_zh: Seven sailors missing after drones strike tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast
articles.content_orig:
Nato source says drones came from Russia, while Romania’s president says attacking commercial ships ‘is unacceptable and has to stop’
Seven sailors are missing after drones struck two tankers near Romania’s Black Sea ⁠coast, setting them ablaze and raising ⁠fresh security concerns on a ​vital shipping route used by Ukraine.
A Nato military source told Reuters the drones that had hit the Wine Trader and the Yara J came from Russia . “The drones that caused ⁠the fires on board two tankers inside Romanian territorial waters were of Russian origin,” the source said.
Romania’s president, Nicușor Dan, described the situation in the Black Sea as serious. “Commercial ships are being attacked and sunk,” he wrote on X. “Seafarers killed, injured and missing very close to the shores of Romania and Bulgaria . This is unacceptable and it has to stop.”
His statement followed a meeting with Bulgaria’s prime minister, Rumen Radev, and Nato’s secretary-general, Mark Rutte, on Thursday, where they agreed “to strengthen our defences in the Black Sea”, Dan said.
Rutte said: “Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed.”
A Nato official said the issue would be discussed at a meeting of the North Atlantic Council next week.
The missing crew were from the Wine Trader, a San Marino-flagged tanker travelling from Tunisia to Romania. All crew on the Yara J, which was struck just inside Romanian waters late on Wednesday, were safe.
Similar incidents in recent weeks have raised fears that the zone is becoming another front in Russia’s war on Ukraine .
Dan said the two ships had been struck by drones, but declined to say whether Russia was responsible.
Romania shares a 614km (381-mile) border with Ukraine, much of it along the Danube. The country has experienced frequent drone incursions since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, including a daytime encroachment last November that led Nato to scramble fighter jets .
after newsletter promotion
EU leaders were already concerned about drone strikes on merchant ships off the coast of Bulgaria. On Tuesday, drone strikes on two ships off the coast of Bulgaria prompted emergency rescue operations, with 11 crew member from the HS Dignity, a cargo ship sailing under a Guinea-Bissau flag, still missing.
On another ship, the Ukrainian-operated Chelsea 3 sailing under a Maltese flag, rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries. The crew reported that the ship’s deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones.
“The results of this attack favour Russia. However, we don’t have any solid evidence that the drones are Russians,” Radev said after arriving in Brussels for an EU summit on Thursday.
At least 23 sailors have been reported missing or killed after attacks on commercial shipping near the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania in the past 10 days, according to Reuters.
Russia has stepped up its bombing campaign on Ukraine’s Black Sea infrastructure, forcing Kyiv to turn to Danube river ports and Black Sea routes off the coasts of Romania and Bulgaria to export its grain, sunflower oil and other products.
According to a draft summit declaration, EU leaders will say that attacks against civilian shipping, including “member state-flagged vessels, such as the recent attacks in Bulgaria’s and Romania’s exclusive economic zones in the Black Sea, are unacceptable and constitute a serious violation of international and maritime law”.

articles.title_orig: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt
articles.title_zh: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt
articles.content_orig:
CoreWeave 's credit stress continued to spiral on Thursday amid a broader sell-off in AI-related names.
CoreWeave — a so-called neocloud company — has taken on more than $51 billion of debt and obligations to finance its AI infrastructure buildout. It's now facing a rebellion from stock and bond investors as concerns mount about AI overspending and debt levels.
Yields on CoreWeave debt have continued to climb, with the yield to maturity on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 reaching 15.78%. Bond yields move inversely to prices. Meanwhile, the spread on its five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, at one point soared above 1,140 basis points. It last stood at 1,088 bps — a 33% week-over-week jump and 177% higher than a year ago.
Credit concerns are spreading into AI equities too. CoreWeave's stock was down again Thursday, adding to Wednesday's 15.5% nosedive .
Other neocloud stocks were under similar pressure. Nebius was down 5% and Iren sank 8% in Thursday trading.
Anxiety about AI overspending is also spreading. For instance, shares of Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices shed 4% and 6%, respectively, following a big sell-off in South Korean chip stocks.
While AI debt worries have been rising steadily, investors have suddenly grown skittish about the underlying finances of companies borrowing heavily to buy chips, build data centers, and rent out computing power.
Coreweave's credit default swaps are one place to see that stress.
Credit default swaps are contracts where buyers pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. The spread widening in CoreWeave's CDS means investors view the debt as riskier.
The market is "basically saying 'no mas' to AI debt without operating cash flow support," the Evercore ISI trading desk said.
A spread level of 1,000 basis points or above is generally a sign of credit distress, said Gavan Nolan, executive director of fixed income pricing at S&P Global Market Intelligence.
No one is questioning whether demand for CoreWeave's services is real, since the company has contracts with all the big hyperscalers, Nolan said. The question is whether the cash flows will ultimately arrive.
"It's obviously heavily negative free cash flow at the moment, and it needs that cash flow to arrive really to justify all the capex that it's spending," Nolan said.
CEO Mike Intrator dismissed the market moves on Wednesday, according to a memo obtained by CNBC.
"When you are building a new type of technology company there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally," he wrote. "We are confident in our backlog which more than supports all of our debt obligations."
The backlog is over $100 billion, with around two-thirds of it with investment-grade counterparts including Microsoft , Meta , IBM and Caterpillar , Deutsche Bank said in a note Thursday. The firm reiterated its buy-rating on the stock Wednesday, calling the dislocation a buying opportunity.
"The problem is this kind of concern can prove to be a self-fulfilling prophecy, and risks triggering broader issues in other AI-related names," said Jim Reid, global head of macro and thematic research.
Domino effects may already be happening. Oracle 's five-year CDS spread also spiked this week. It was last at 288 basis points, a more than 12% increase in one week.
"A downgrade from its BBB rating would risk pressuring IG-only investors into forced sales," Reid said.

articles.title_zh: Watch: 99-year-old woman becomes world's oldest wing walker
articles.content_orig:
Oct. 15 (UPI) -- A British woman celebrated her 99th birthday by going wing walking -- and becoming the oldest person to ever do the stunt.
Helga Duffy said she was inspired to attempt the Guinness World Record for the world's oldest wing walker when she news coverage of previous record-holder Betty Bromage performing the feat at the age of 97.
Duffy's wing walk was originally set to take place on her birthday, Sept. 23, but was delayed to Oct. 16.
A Guinness World Records adjudicator was present at RFC Rendcomb Airfield in Cirencester, Gloucestershire, to confirm Duffy's record and present her with a certificate.
The record attempt raised money for Wiltshire and Bath Air Ambulance.
Bromage offered her congratulations to the new record-holder, but indicated she might retake the title.
"I can't wait until I'm 100 and I can do it again, I'll beat you again," she told the BBC.

articles.title_orig: Time’s up for ‘leap second’ thanks to Earth’s accelerating spin
articles.title_zh: Time’s up for ‘leap second’ thanks to Earth’s accelerating spin
articles.content_orig:
International delegates agree leap second no longer tenable, but first leap hour not likely to happen for thousands of years
A fter decades of discussion, quibbling and worrying about clocks in computer systems, the world’s official timekeepers have voted to replace what many viewed as a tiresome correction: the leap second. It’s time, they say, for the leap hour.
Delegates from 69 countries cast their votes on Thursday at a conference in France of the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, which ensures the world sticks to the same standards of time, weight, distance and more.
The decision to adopt the leap hour from next year aims to reduce the risk of computers and other technical systems tripping over as their software grapples with minutes lasting 61 seconds – and, worse, 59 seconds – instead of a round 60.
“After 30 years of debate, the leap second is making way for the leap hour,” said Dr Setnam Shemar, principal scientist in the time and frequency department at the UK’s National Physical Laboratory (NPL). “This will reduce the risks to the systems and national infrastructure that depend on accurate time while still preserving the fundamental link between our global time system and the rotation of the Earth.”
The vote at Versailles means that coordinated universal time (UTC) can drift up to an hour from astronomical time before a leap hour is needed, but that is unlikely to happen for thousands of years.
“We already have daylight saving where we change by an hour and no one gets bothered about that, apart from losing sleep or getting an extra hour’s sleep,” said Shemar, who sat on the international timekeeping expert committee that proposed the leap hour.
The more familiar leap year was introduced more than 2,000 years ago to ensure that the calendar year did not fall out of step with the time that the Earth takes to circle the sun. Adding a day to the end of February every four or so years does the job, because Earth orbits the sun every 365 and a quarter days.
Leap seconds are a much more modern invention. In 1955, Louis Essen and Jack Parry at the NPL built the world’s first practical, high-precision caesium atomic clock. The device revolutionised timekeeping, and in 1967 the astronomical definition of a second, based on the rotation of the Earth, was abandoned. Ever since, the formal definition of one second has been 9,192,631,770 vibrations of the caesium atom.
Atomic clocks are exceptionally stable and precise. Their timekeeping has become critical for modern computer systems, communications, satellites, trading systems and electricity grids. But the Earth’s rotation is far less reliable. Its spin is affected by the planet’s molten core, the shift of the oceans, global jet streams and other natural forces.
Broadly, Earth’s rotation is slowing down: when an asteroid doomed the dinosaurs, a day lasted about 23 and a half hours. Because of this, officials have added 27 leap seconds since 1972 to ensure UTC is aligned with astronomical time.
The strategy endured for more than 50 years until scientists spotted a fresh reason to fear technological mayhem. In the past decade, Earth’s rotation has sped up, meaning officials might have needed to add the first negative leap second, equivalent to lopping a second off UTC. The 30% probability of a negative leap second in the next decade brought the Versailles vote forward.
“Leap seconds can be tricky enough to deal with,” said Shemar. Telecommunications, electricity grids and navigation systems used high-accuracy timing, he explained, but software updates could apply leap seconds at the wrong time, knocking networks out of sync.
after newsletter promotion
“After the leap second applied in 2012, there were some computer systems whose operating systems couldn’t cope with 61 seconds in a minute. The servers froze, they seized up. Systems went offline. And those are the sorts of failures that can happen with positive leap seconds,” Shemar said.
Among the crashed websites were Reddit and LinkedIn. Separately, Qantas flights were hit with delays. Negative leap seconds come with even greater risks. “There could be software out there that hasn’t been tested on negative leap seconds because we’ve never had to apply one before,” Shemar said.
To test all the computer systems that talk to one another around the world would cost companies a fortune. It was this concern that swung the vote.
Historically, the UK has grumbled about canning leap seconds because of the link with Greenwich mean time. Russia has also opposed the move, citing concerns of the impact on its Glonass satellite navigation system.
The IERS Earth Orientation Centre, in Paris, tracks changes in the Earth’s rotation and other movements that feed into UTC. The centre also issues notices when leap seconds must be added.
Dr Christian Bizouard, the director of the centre, approved of the vote, but said it passed the decision to people far in the future. “It’s kind of a philosophical discussion, because if a leap hour happens, it won’t be for a very, very long time,” he said. “What we are doing is pushing back the decision.”

articles.title_orig: Alzheimer's Drug ARIA Monitoring: Real-World Study Results
articles.title_zh: Alzheimer's Drug ARIA Monitoring: Real-World Study Results
articles.content_orig:
— Collaboration between prescribers and radiologists is key, lecanemab data show
October 15, 2026 • 3 min read
Rates of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) in Alzheimer's disease patients treated with lecanemab (Leqembi) in the real world were consistent with those seen in clinical trials, data from the LEADER study showed.
Anti-amyloid drugs like lecanemab require MRI monitoring for ARIA, making prescriber-radiologist collaboration essential, said Daryl Rhys Jones, PhD, of drugmaker Eisai in Nutley, New Jersey, at the American Society of Functional Neuroradiology meeting in Newport Beach, California.
ARIA is a consequence of amyloid in blood vessel walls. Two types of ARIA can emerge after anti-amyloid drug treatment: ARIA with edema or effusion (ARIA-E) or ARIA with hemosiderin or hemorrhage (ARIA-H).
In the real-world LEADER study, ARIA rates appeared to be lower than rates seen in the phase III CLARITY AD trial of lecanemab, though the differences may not be significant:
The median time to ARIA-E was 3.4 months, Jones reported. Results were similar between 1.5T and 3T MRI. "This suggests that the power of MRI is not really making a difference in detection, at least in the real world," he told MedPage Today.
ARIA rates in LEADER were consistent with other real-world evidence, including data from the ALZ-NET registry , he added.
Lecanemab, an antibody directed against aggregated soluble and insoluble forms of amyloid beta, was approved in 2023 to treat mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease and mild Alzheimer's dementia. The drug carries a boxed warning that ARIA-E or ARIA-H can occur, with a notice that APOE4 homozygotes have a higher incidence of ARIA than heterozygotes and noncarriers.
ARIA is often asymptomatic, and in rare cases, it can be fatal. Lecanemab prescribing information calls for MRI at baseline, then after 1, 2, 3, and 6 months of treatment to monitor for ARIA.
LEADER is an ongoing, multisite, retrospective study that evaluates lecanemab in clinical settings. It incorporates surveys and interviews with healthcare practitioners with chart and electronic medical record data for up to 50 patients per site.
This interim analysis was based on data from 432 patients with early Alzheimer's disease. All participants received at least seven biweekly lecanemab infusions. Some received intravenous (IV) or subcutaneous maintenance treatment after 18 months of IV initiation treatment. Participants had an average of 520.7 days on lecanemab and an average of 25.8 doses.
The LEADER study includes diverse real-world settings, Jones noted. "We didn't just select academic centers that might have extensive experience," he said. "There are general neurologists included in LEADER who were not part of CLARITY AD, so they were treating these patients for the first time. Yet, they were able to implement lecanemab and successfully monitor for the safety of lecanemab in their patients."
Close prescriber-radiologist collaboration was key to that success, Jones observed. This meant establishing communication between neurologists and radiologists  --  "not just themselves, but their front staff, who might be involved with scheduling, and the administrative team at the site," he said.
"It is very important ... to ensure that the radiologist understood what was needed, because the neurologist needs to know, OK, there is no ARIA, I can continue with treatment, or OK, there is ARIA, but this is asymptomatic and mild," Jones pointed out. There needs to be "very clear guidance to the neuroradiologist about what they should be describing for the neurologist," he said.
The analysis included 12 LEADER sites, "but we've expanded now to 20 sites and we're expanding our patient numbers as well," Jones noted. "And, importantly, we're now looking at subcutaneous administration," he added, which the FDA approved earlier this year.

articles.title_orig: ANALYSIS: Houthis escalate attacks on Saudi Arabia as China suspected of assisting
articles.title_zh: ANALYSIS: Houthis escalate attacks on Saudi Arabia as China suspected of assisting
articles.content_orig:
Middle East expert Behnam Ben Taleblu ties Houthi airport attacks to Iranian threats and warns of possible Russian involvement.
Iran-backed Houthis launched a series of attacks on Saudi Arabian airports through Sunday, reportedly killing at least 14 people, including an American, and injuring more than 300 others, according to reports .
The attacks heightened fears of a wider Middle East war as regional experts warned of "cross-domain escalation" amid heightened tensions over Washington's September actions against Iran's aviation sector.
The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while U.S. officials blamed the Iran-backed group for Saturday's strike, which reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300.
SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE
Smoke and flames rise from King Khalid International Airport after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said they attacked the airport, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Oct. 8, 2026. (Reuters)
Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said another attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others. Meanwhile, an airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also reportedly targeted by the Houthis.
"Cross-domain escalation by Iran and its proxies will continue to be a primary strategy," Behnam Ben Taleblu , senior director of the Iran Program and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Sunday.
"The emphasis on aviation targets connects directly to the closing of Iran's aviation sector and sanctions imposed on its commercial airlines under the U.S. maximum pressure campaign," he warned.

"This rapid targeting reflects earlier threats made by Iranian officials, including a veiled threat from the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warning that U.S. sanctions on Iran's aviation sector would lead to retaliatory threats against neighboring aviation infrastructure," Taleblu said.

The escalation has also renewed scrutiny of reports that Russia has provided intelligence and technical assistance to the Houthis.

But he also linked the latest attacks to a broader military escalation as the Houthis expand their territorial control in Yemen.

articles.title_orig: Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Trailer
articles.title_zh: Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Trailer
articles.content_orig:
Rockstar Games has revealed that Justice composed the original score for Grand Theft Auto VI . Today the French electronic duo have also shared their contribution to the video game’s expansive soundtrack. “ Flower in a Hurricane ” features a bonkers trifecta of Tame Impala , SZA , and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard , and you can hear snippets of it in the new GTA VI launch trailer below.
The last Grand Theft Auto score, way back in 2013, was a collaborative effort between the Alchemist, Tangerine Dream, Woody Jackson, and Oh No, mixed and synced by DJ Shadow. Justice take up the mantle following the release of their last LP, 2024’s Hyperdrama . That album’s “ Neverender ,” another Tame Impala team-up, nabbed them a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Recording in 2025.
The 34-track GTA VI soundtrack is being slow-rolled ahead of its official release alongside the game on November 19. So far there have been nine songs released, including contributions from Yung Lean , Travis Scott , and Cardi B . Last week, Rockstar also unveiled the in-game radio DJs for GTA VI . Soon enough, you’ll be able to tune in to Bad Bunny’s Cocoteo FM, Robyn’s Flash FM, Lana Del Rey’s Back Country Radio, and more.

articles.title_orig: Man shot by ICE in NYC's Marble Hill said federal officers never identified themselves
articles.title_zh: Man shot by ICE in NYC's Marble Hill said federal officers never identified themselves
articles.content_orig:

The man shot and wounded by federal immigration agents in Marble Hill last week says that he didn’t know that the men who ambushed and shot him were U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents until he later woke up in the hospital.
A new petition filed in Brooklyn federal court on Oscar Belgal's behalf includes key details that contradict the Trump administration’s version of the events. Belgal claims in the filing on Wednesday that the ICE agents involved — many of them masked — didn’t identify themselves before approaching his vehicle with firearms drawn.
“The men did not identify themselves, show any documents or otherwise communicate with Oscar in any substantive way,” according to the filing. Last week, U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters that the agents identified themselves as they approached Belgal’s vehicle in the Oct. 8 encounter on a busy street. “ There was no question he would've known who was approaching,” Mullin said.
The petition also says that Belgal “vehemently denies” any relationship to any gang or organized criminal group. Top ICE and DHS officials claimed Belgal was part of the Trinitarios gang, and said that is why he was targeted for arrest.
The petition also states that Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican immigrant, received no aid from the federal agents, even as he pleaded for medical assistance. The petition states that Belgal was not trying to ram his vehicle into officers. Federal officials claimed Belgal was fired upon after he “weaponized his vehicle” and tried to ram into officers.
A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that Belgal’s arrest was justified because he was in the country without authorization, and that Belgal disobeyed ICE agents' commands during the incident and fled from law enforcement. The government was given a Monday deadline to respond.
The petition advocating for Belgal’s immediate release from ICE custody replaces a previous petition filed on Belgal’s behalf in Manhattan shortly after his arrest.
The new petition provides the clearest picture yet of Belgal's version of the events. Moments before he was shot, Belgal had picked up his 5-year-old son from school and taken him to McDonald’s for a snack, according to the petition.
Belgal parked in a spot near his Marble Hill home, but he began to pull out as he realized it was in front of a fire hydrant, the petition states. That’s when an armed man dressed in civilian clothing and wearing black face coverings “bolted toward his vehicle,” according to the new court filing. Several other men followed, wearing masks and holding weapons.
The men — who Belgal said he only later learned were ICE agents — did not appear to be law enforcement or identify themselves as immigration agents, the petition states. They did not present him with an arrest warrant, say his name or provide any other substantive explanation for the encounter as they confronted him through his partially rolled-down car window, the filing states. One of the agents pointed a weapon inside the car, leaving Belgal “terrified” for his and his son’s lives, according to the filing.
Belgal’s attorneys said in the petition that one officer struck the driver’s side window and shattered the glass, which exploded on Belgal’s face and arm. The agent then fired at least seven shots into the car while Belgal’s son “cowered in the back seat,” according to the petition.
Marcos Charles, the executive associate director of ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations wing, last week alleged that Belgal “ weaponized his vehicle ” against the agents as they tried to arrest him. But in the new filing, Belgal’s attorneys said video footage “clearly shows” that he was trying to pull his car forward, where no officers were stationed at the time, to get away from the officer who was shooting into his vehicle. The attorneys said another car then “careened from behind and blocked the path.”
After a bullet hit Belgal in the neck, he got out of his car and “pleaded for medical assistance, fearing that he was dying,” the filing states. His son screamed that the masked men had killed his father, according to the petition.
The petition states the officers threw Belgal down, handcuffed him, pinned him to the car and left him slumped over as he faded in and out of consciousness, rather than providing medical aid. It also accuses ICE agents of failing to take any steps to get him to a hospital — noting that it was NYPD officers who took him to get medical care.
Belgal didn’t realize until he woke up in the hospital that the men who confronted him with guns drawn were immigration agents, his attorneys said. In his hospital bed, ICE officers handcuffed him, according to the petition.
Doctors told Belgal that he needed surgery to remove the bullet and that he should come back for surgery the next week, the filing states. After his release from the hospital, immigration officials took him to New Jersey for the night, then to the Metropolitan Detention Center in Sunset Park, his attorneys said.
Last week, a federal judge ordered that Belgal not be removed from the country or transferred outside of the New York City metro area or New Jersey for the time being.
While in ICE detention, Belgal "replays the traumatic events of Oct. 8 over and over in his memory, with his son’s hysterical cries ringing endlessly in his head,” the petition states.
Belgal's son didn't speak for several days after seeing his father shot, and suffers daily from nightmares, according to the petition.
This story was updated with additional information.

articles.title_orig: Albania's leader defies calls to resign as student protesters rampage in capital
articles.title_zh: Albania's leader defies calls to resign as student protesters rampage in capital
articles.content_orig:
Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Thursday rejected calls to resign as thousands of student-led protesters smashed windows and fought running battles with riot police firing water cannon and tear gas in the capital.
Protesters voiced anger about perceived corruption, the cost and quality of education and a deal to sell off parts of its pristine southern coastline to a luxury resort development backed by US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.
They demanded Rama’s resignation, saying no one had listened to their concerns during a summer of largely peaceful protests over the development.
In a written statement to Reuters, Rama rejected calls to quit.
Student protests in Albania lead to clashes with police
“My responsibility is to listen, address legitimate concerns and keep Albania moving forward. The alternative would be a betrayal of the Albanians who gave me a strong mandate to complete negotiations on European Union membership,” he said.
A student who gave her name as Kiara said the cost of living, poor job prospects, and alleged corruption were the main issues.
“Our prime minister is the meaning of the word corruption. You can only find work in your field if you know a guy who knows a guy,” she said, her face covered by a mask, like many on the streets on Thursday.
The protests, now in their third day, mark the biggest challenge yet to Rama, who won a fourth term last year, with E.U. membership at the center of his campaign. Parliament cancelled its session as the violence erupted again nearby.
Rama, whose government denies corruption, said he would be ready to discuss the rising cost of education, but added: “Attacking institutions, destroying public property and threatening public safety have nothing to do with the legitimate demands of students.”
Tirana’s streets were littered with burned out garbage bins, shattered bus stops and broken traffic lights.
Wafts of tear gas drifted across the center. Protesters hurled stones at police, who used water cannon to push protesters back. In the central Skanderbeg Square, police hit fleeing protesters with batons as tourists looked on.
“This government is corrupted, led and governed by a corrupt prime minister,” protester Lulzim Tanushi, a lawyer, said. “Since Rama came to power he has abused and ruined people’s lives and that is why people are showing their anger — when they were not heard before.”
The protests follow months of mostly peaceful demonstrations sparked by the plans to build the resort, which has faced legal challenges.
Villagers told Reuters in July that their land was wrongfully sold for development. Reuters later reported that the man who sold the land was wanted by prosecutors for drug trafficking, charges his lawyer denied.
Reuters found no evidence of wrongdoing by Kushner, who is not directly involved in the villagers’ dispute.
Albania’s image has been tarnished over the years by corruption scandals and political analysts say the country is a hub for gangs seeking to launder money from drugs and weapons trafficking, complicating its efforts to join the E.U.
Along with Montenegro, Albania is currently leading the accession process among Balkan countries and is aiming for entry as early as 2028.
“Corruption must be confronted and, as the E.U. itself has recently reaffirmed, Albania is tackling it as never before,” Rama said to Reuters.
“Perhaps some forces, at home and abroad, do not want Albania to succeed as a forerunner for E.U. membership. But I will not allow violence to derail Albania’s European future.”
A European Union mission to Albania in a statement on X said: “Constructive dialogue is the only way forward.”
The unrest is part of a wave of student activism in Europe. In France, high school students have staged weeks of protests and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education.

Jackie, a beloved bald eagle who become an internet sensation and a symbol of the species' recovery, died of bird flu, wildlife officials say.
A necropsy and further testing identified highly pathogenic avian influenza as the primary underlying cause of her death in August, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife said Wednesday.
In the weeks before her death, Jackie was receiving care at the Ojai Raptor Center for various ailments, including anemia.
Chris Eksteen, the center's director, said in the news release that the necropsy results “have helped connect many of the findings” they saw during her hospitalization.
“In an uncommon presentation of the virus, the infection caused a severe ulcer in her stomach that led to persistent internal bleeding, anemia, and the development of bacterial sepsis," Steve Kubiski, the disease investigations director at the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, where the necropsy was conducted, added in the news release.
Nature lovers watched Jackie and her partner, Shadow, tend to their nest in trees near Big Bear Lake for more than a decade via an online video feed. The nest camera, located in the San Bernardino Mountains east of Los Angeles, was installed in 2015 by the nonprofit Friends of Big Bear Valley, which documented the successes and failures of each breeding season.
Highly pathogenic avian influenza has been circulating in bird populations throughout the US. There is no evidence Shadow is ill, according to the news release.
Waterfowl and shorebirds are natural hosts for bird flu viruses, but eagles and other raptors can be exposed through contact with infected birds or by eating them, according to the news release.
Jackie's remains were cremated to prevent transmission of the virus, it said.
American bald eagles teetered on the brink of extinction until the pesticide DDT was banned in the 1970s and other protections were established. The species rebounded and was removed from the federal endangered list.

articles.title_orig: Texas resident finds second world war-era grenades in box bought at estate sale
articles.title_zh: Texas resident finds second world war-era grenades in box bought at estate sale
articles.content_orig:
Discovery of grenades prompted a neighborhood lockdown and a visit from the Austin police department’s bomb squad
A buyer at a Texas estate sale discovered several second world war-era grenades in a box of newly bought items, prompting a neighbourhood lockdown and a visit from the Austin police department’s bomb squad.
The grenades, which were described as “live and active” in a social media post by the Austin police association, were removed and disarmed.
Their age and apparent volatility, the post said, required delicate handling by bomb squad members whose “training, expertise, and steady nerves” were rarely seen by the public.
“Handling 80-year-old explosives with unknown stability is dangerous, precise work, and they do it with the professionalism this city counts on,” the post said.
“Huge thanks to our patrol officers, who quickly secured the scene, set up a perimeter, and kept neighbors safe while they waited for EOD [explosive ordinance disposal].”
The police association did not identify the seller or buyer of the box of grenades, and said the person who bought them made the discovery only as he was rifling through several boxes of his new items on Monday.
“No crime here,” the post said. “Just a great reminder, if you ever come across old military ordnance (grenades, shells, mortar rounds, etc), even if you think it’s inert, don’t touch it, don’t move it, and call 911.
“Let the experts handle it.”
Austin’s KLBJ news station identified at least three of the olive-colored grenades as Mk 2 anti-personnel fragmentation grenades , widely used by US forces during the second world war, and known as “pineapple” grenades because of their distinctive shape.
The grenades were still in limited use with the US army and Marine Corps until the 1960s.
The station said bomb squad technicians examined the highly explosive devices with X-rays and determined they were live, but did not pose an immediate threat under the circumstances.
The Guardian reported earlier this month on the dangers specialist teams face in dealing with decades-old unexploded ordinance, including the degradation of fuses and increasing instability of explosives over time.
It followed the discovery of two large, unexploded German bombs found separately in the UK county of Devon, one on a floating dredger and another on a building site. Experts said the devices “could knock a whole street down”.

articles.title_orig: Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 Review: The Prettiest, Most Comfortable Handheld You Can Buy
articles.title_zh: Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 Review: The Prettiest, Most Comfortable Handheld You Can Buy
articles.content_orig:
A celebration of the ROG brand, the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 is a cool collector's item, with a great new OLED screen and an eye-catching design. However, with performance that's about the same as last year's Xbox Ally X, it's a hard sell at $1,299.
Due to the ongoing RAM crisis , handheld gaming PCs have long parted ways with affordability. But that hasn't stopped vendors like Asus from putting out revisions to their existing lineups. The latest is the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 ($1,299), a swanky gold-and-black repackaging of last year's Editors' Choice-award-winning Asus ROG Xbox Ally X . Now it has a translucent chassis, custom gold RGB lighting, and an illuminated Xbox button, all in celebration of the Asus ROG brand's 20th anniversary.
In terms of specs, the Xbox Ally X20 is identical to the older model: It offers the same impressive AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme processor, ergonomics, and dimensions. If you bought the Xbox Ally X last year, then there's no real reason to upgrade, unless you're intrigued by the new OLED panel. However, given the price, it's hard to fully recommend this handheld unless you've got cash to burn. In terms of pure power, the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is a better choice, though it's even more expensive. Yes, the Xbox Ally X20's pricing leaves it caught between a rock and a hard place, but it's still a very capable handheld gaming PC and a fun collector's item if you're willing to splurge.
Now, I don't mean to sound too glum while talking about the Xbox Ally X20; I really liked the previous version, the Xbox Ally X, when I reviewed it last year. The Xbox Ally X has the best ergonomics of the many handheld gaming PCs I've reviewed (it even tops the Nintendo Switch 2 in that regard), thanks to the contoured grips that frame the system. That's true of the Xbox X20, too, as it shares the same design principles. They distribute weight evenly and have a slight texture that not only feels good but also adds extra grip.
The machine's measurements are exactly the same, as well. The Xbox Ally X20 measures at 1.9 by 11.8 by 4.7 inches (HWD), just slightly wider than the Steam Deck OLED (1.9 by 11.7 by 4.6 inches HWD). Regarding weight, the Xbox Ally X20 weighs in at 1.6 pounds, slightly heavier than the Xbox Ally X but far lighter than the Lenovo Legion Go 2 and the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+. That's not quite as light as the Steam Deck OLED's 1.4 pounds or the Switch 2's 1.18 pounds.
Curious about the Xbox Ally X20 newer aspects? Let's start with the translucent chassis. It's a callback to the "xtreme" see-through electronics of the late 1990s and early 2000s, a gaming trend that I welcome. From the front, you can admire some of the machine's innards; from the back, you can appreciate the motherboard and fans peeking through the machine's vents.
Two gold buttons flank the Xbox Ally X20’s mighty 7.4-inch screen, while the Xbox button, nestled between the left control stick and the Command Center and View buttons, now glows Xbox green. It's not as bright as the RGB rings that wrap around both control sticks, but it certainly pops against the system's black color. And if you look closely, you can still see the "Xbox ROG" lettering trickling down the handheld. At the system level, the celebration continues with a custom 20th-anniversary startup logo, wallpaper, and screensaver.
Turn it around, and you’ll spot the 20th anniversary gold badge among Asus ROG’s typical design language. Two macro buttons sit just in reach of your middle and index fingers, and the slightly textured shoulder buttons are pleasant to the touch. They feel good to press, too, thanks to the Hall-effect analog triggers. Aesthetically, the Xbox Ally X20 is far more visually pleasing than the plain black original, and the handheld comes with a simple cardboard stand for showcasing it on your desk or for monitor use. (It lacks a kickstand.)
Undeniably, the biggest change between the two Xbox-branded systems is the display. The first change is one you might not notice at first glance. The Xbox Ally X20's screen is 0.4 inch bigger than the Xbox Ally X's 7-inch screen. The second, and most obvious, is that the Xbox Ally X20 upgrades to an OLED screen. Both systems still offer a 1,920-by-1,080-pixel resolution with a 16:9 aspect ratio and a 120Hz refresh rate. But the OLED has improved brightness (600 nits, versus the Ally X's 500 nits).
The Xbox Ally X20 also offers HDR support, which wasn't in the original model. With HDR on, Asus says that the system can reach a max brightness of 1,400 nits. It's also officially Pantone Validated, a certification program that ensures the machine can faithfully reproduce colors from the Pantone Matching System (PMS) . And finally, the screen supports AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, an update over the Xbox Ally X's AMD FreeSync Premium. In addition to suppressing screen tearing, the Pro upgrade adds color and luminance certification as well as HDR compatibility.
Rounding out the system's specs, you'll find the Xbox Ally X20 comes equipped with 24GB of DDR5 memory and a 1TB M.2 solid-state drive. Two USB-C ports are on the top of the handheld (one USB-C 3.2 and one USB4 ), both supporting Power Delivery 3.0 and DisplayPort 2.1 output. The USB4 port is also Thunderbolt-compatible. A 3.5mm headphone jack is there for audio. It’s all virtually the same as on the Xbox Ally X, except for the microSD card reader. It's now a microSD Express card slot, an improvement from the Ally's UHS-II microSD card reader, which means that you can expect faster read and write speeds with the Xbox Ally X20.
One of the things that made the original Xbox Ally X such a big deal at launch was the introduction of the Xbox Full Screen Experience (now simply called Xbox Mode). It's Microsoft's attempt to bring the Xbox console experience to handhelds and make the Windows handheld experience comparable to Valve's excellent SteamOS.
Xbox Mode returns with the Xbox Ally X20, and using it has perks. It makes navigation easier and aggregates your game library, including titles downloaded from stores other than Microsoft's. Even better, Xbox Mode uses less RAM. That's because it pushes Windows 11 into the background, cutting all Windows processes to only the most essential for maximum game performance.
Xbox Mode is still the best way to play your games on a Windows handheld, and while things have gotten easier, there are still many quirks and glitches that sometimes don't resolve themselves without a full reset. For example, sometimes I'll turn on the Xbox Ally X20 and get ready to enter my four-digit password. However, the system won't detect my button presses or screen taps. A reset sets things right, but that this issue still remains a year later is annoying, even if it's minor.
SteamOS also tucks away its desktop in the back end. As many people, including myself, have discovered, Windows 11 is quite a heavy processing load on handheld gaming PCs. While testing the SteamOS version of the Lenovo Legion Go S (running the Z2 Go chip), I discovered that ditching Windows 11 significantly improves game performance. In fact, testing Cyberpunk 2077 on both the Windows 11 and SteamOS variants of the Legion Go S, the SteamOS version delivered a 69% performance boost over the Windows 11 version. Although Asus retained Windows 11 here, Xbox Mode is a way for Microsoft to at least try to reckon with that reality.
Upon Xbox Mode's debut, Microsoft promised features that were not quite ready at launch. The most significant was Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), a system-level feature that uses the Ryzen NPU's power to upscale games running at lower resolutions, much like AMD's FSR, thereby freeing resources for graphics rendering during docked-mode play. It finally launched a few months ago, so I tested it to see how it uses the Ryzen NPU.
To activate it, you first must be an Xbox Insider member. If you're enrolled, you can turn on Auto SR in two ways. You can either enable it in Windows Settings (System > Dis

articles.title_orig: Social Security cost-of-living increase sparks debate over looming funding shortfall
articles.title_zh: Social Security cost-of-living increase sparks debate over looming funding shortfall
articles.content_orig:
Michael A. Peterson, CEO of the Peter G. Peterson Foundation, discusses the fiscal challenges facing the U.S. and why policymakers need to pursue solutions.
Social Security beneficiaries could face a 22% across-the-board benefit reduction in 2032 without congressional action, according to the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFB), as a new cost-of-living adjustment renews debate over the program's financial future.
The warning comes as Social Security's retirement trust fund approaches a projected 2032 depletion date, putting pressure on lawmakers to address the program's long-term funding shortfall.
Social Security recipients will receive a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment in 2027, raising the average retired worker's monthly benefit by about $75, from $2,095 to $2,170, according to estimates cited by AARP.
The increase, announced by the Social Security Administration on Wednesday, will take effect with December benefits, which are paid in January.
US REGULATOR ACCUSES NATION'S LARGEST BANKS OF DEBANKING CUSTOMERS OVER POLITICAL VIEWS
Two people enter a Social Security Administration office in suburban Detroit. (Jim West/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)
The 2027 increase is the highest COLA in four years and compares with a 2.8% adjustment this year. It reflects inflation readings from the third quarter, including a 3.9% year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers in September.
The boost comes as many older Americans continue to face higher costs for groceries, utilities, insurance and healthcare. The standard Medicare Part B premium is also projected to rise by $6.60 per month in 2027, to $209.50, according to AARP.
CRFB estimates the 3.6% adjustment will add about $900 annually to the average retiree's benefits, even as the program's projected funding shortfall raises questions about the sustainability of future payments.
A woman walks into a Social Security office in Houston, Texas, on July 13, 2022. (Mark Felix/The Washington Post / Getty Images)
But the increase will not be distributed equally in dollar terms. CRFB estimates that while the average retiree will receive about $900 more annually, the highest-benefit recipients could see increases exceeding $2,200. The group said the highest-earning couples who retired this year at normal retirement age could receive a combined $3,600 increase, pushing their annual benefits above $100,000.
AMERICA'S $40T NATIONAL DEBT IS ‘STEALING FROM OUR NEXT GENERATION,’ ECONOMIST WARNS
The larger dollar increases come amid a broader generational economic divide. A Federal Reserve report released in May found that just 63% of adults ages 18 to 29 reported doing okay financially or living comfortably in 2025, compared with 83% of adults ages 60 and older. Nearly half of adults under 30 received financial assistance from someone outside their household to cover expenses during the year.
An eagle tops the U.S. Federal Reserve building's facade in Washington, July 31, 2013. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters)
The financial pressures facing younger Americans add another dimension to the debate over Social Security's future. Current workers help fund the program through payroll taxes, even as its retirement trust fund faces a projected shortfall. According to the Social Security trustees' 2026 report, the fund is expected to exhaust its reserves in 2032, leaving continuing income sufficient to cover about 78% of scheduled retirement and survivor benefits without changes to the law.
CRFB has advocated for changes to the way COLAs are calculated, including using a different inflation measure or placing a dollar cap on increases for higher-income beneficiaries. The group also supports additional revenue and other benefit reforms to improve the program's finances.

AARP, however, opposes proposals to reduce or cap annual COLAs, arguing that the adjustments already fall short of keeping pace with the costs older Americans face.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX Stock Drops: Starlink Ukraine Risks Are a Problem for Musk
articles.title_zh: SpaceX Stock Drops: Starlink Ukraine Risks Are a Problem for Musk
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk said Wednesday that the U.S. government and President Donald Trump are responsible for any curbs on Ukraine's military-grade Starlink network.
Writing on X, Musk said that "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Ukraine had accused SpaceX of imposing new restrictions on the Starshield internet service without warning, leading to disruptions to Ukrainian military operations amid fresh Russian strikes on its energy infrastructure.
On Wednesday, Serhii Beskrestnov, an advisor to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on defense technology, said SpaceX had implemented a speed limit on Starlink terminals in motion, without notifying the country's defense forces.
That had disrupted some missions, and the same restrictions also applied to Starshield, he said on Telegram . Starlink is used to operate Ukraine's interceptor drones, the "most effective solution" against Moscow's Shahed drones, Beskrestnov said.
Starshield is a military-grade satellite network, while Starlink is only meant for "civilian or defensive activities," Musk said.
Some restrictions appear to have been partially lifted, with former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov thanking Musk early Thursday morning that Starlink connectivity at speeds of up to 160 kilometers an hour had been restored. "Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine's defense," Fedorov added.
The developments come amid tensions between Kyiv and Washington over an "energy ceasefire," between Ukraine and Russia announced by Trump.
Ukraine has, however, welcomed a deal subject to Moscow honoring its commitment, while Russian authorities said talks were ongoing, without confirming whether they had reached an agreement. On Monday, Zelenskyy accused the Russians of breaching the ceasefire.
Trump had also taken aim at Ukraine as it continues to strike Russian energy facilities, saying that Kyiv's attacks were responsible for the increase in diesel prices, instead of the U.S.' war with Iran.
Washington has threatened to cut intelligence sharing with Kyiv, Reuters reported Wednesday, while Ukrainian officials said a day earlier that they have not received warnings of Russian attacks on the country for two straight days.
— CNBC's Elsa Olhen contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: NASA-backed mission aims to land on Mars moon, bring samples home
articles.title_zh: NASA-backed mission aims to land on Mars moon, bring samples home
articles.content_orig:
NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet.
The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20).
“The samples from MMX will bring forth paradigm-shifting science on the Mars system for generations to come, especially as NASA prepares to send the first humans to Mars,” said Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “The NASA-JAXA sample curation partnership is extremely valuable, and I am proud that NASA Science is supporting MMX sample curation and will be sharing portions of these samples for study as we continue to expand humanity’s understanding of the universe for the benefit of all.”
NASA’s contributions to the mission include the Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma rays and Neutrons (MEGANE) spectrograph instrument, the Pneumatic Sampler (P-Sampler) technology demonstration, and communications and navigation support from the agency’s Deep Space Network , as well as funding United States scientists participating on the MMX science team.
Scientists have long debated the origin of Mars’ two moons. The data and samples collected by the MMX mission will help answer essential questions about the origins of these moons and the history of the solar system.
“Phobos and Deimos may be the remains of a massive impact on Mars that sent material into orbit around the planet, or they could be ancient asteroids that were captured by Mars’ gravity billions of years ago,” said Tom Statler, MMX program executive and program scientist at NASA Headquarters. “Having the answer will help illuminate that early era when Earth and the other inner planets may have been acquiring much of their water and organic compounds.”
The MEGANE (pronounced meh-GAH-nay, the Japanese word for eyeglasses) spectrograph will help scientists “see” what Phobos is made of by measuring neutrons and gamma rays emitted from the moon’s surface and determining its chemical elemental composition, which will provide important clues about its origin.
Mounted on one of the spacecraft’s landing legs, the P-Sampler is designed to collect a ground sample from Phobos. The system gathers surface material using bursts of high-pressure nitrogen gas, complementing JAXA’s C-Sampler, which will extract cores from a few inches deeper. NASA will obtain and curate about 15% of the total returned sample at the agency’s Johnson Space Center Astromaterials Lab in Houston, making it available for research for decades.
Another key part of NASA’s contribution to MMX is its scientific partnership with JAXA. NASA-supported researchers are working alongside international colleagues to help reveal the story of Phobos and will use mission data and returned samples to uncover new clues about the moon’s origin and the evolution of the Mars system.
The MMX spacecraft will arrive at Mars in August 2027 to begin its survey of the Red Planet’s two moons. After surveying Phobos in detail, the spacecraft will collect a sample of the moon’s surface no earlier than December 2028 and deliver it to Earth in 2031.
The MEGANE instrument was developed by the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory. Honeybee Robotics, a Blue Origin company, developed the spacecraft’s pneumatic sampler mechanism. NASA’s contributions to the MMX mission were developed under the agency’s Discovery Program. The Discovery Program is managed by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, for the agency’s Science Mission Directorate in Washington.
For more information about the MMX mission, visit:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mmx

articles.title_orig: Trump ripped for reaction to Pope Leo cancer diagnosis: ‘Incapable of giving a s—t’
articles.title_zh: Trump ripped for reaction to Pope Leo cancer diagnosis: ‘Incapable of giving a s—t’
articles.content_orig:
A banner reading "Ematology greets the pope" hangs from a window of the Agostino Gemelli Polyclinic where Pope Leo XIV is hospitalised, in Rome, Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. (AP/Alessandra Tarantino)
Send your thoughts to Letters to the Editor . Learn more
Pope Leo XIV met with a top aide on Thursday and resumed working from the hospital, as doctors reported his lung had recovered well from surgery to remove a cancerous nodule .
Leo's post-operative tests remained within normal levels and his physiotherapy session Thursday involved full mobility exercises, with the pope going about his daily activities independently, said the update from Leo's personal doctor, Dr. Luigi Carbone, and the head of thoracic surgery at Gemelli hospital, Dr. Stefano Margaritora.
"The chest X-ray revealed good recovery of the operated lung," they reported. "Overall, his postoperative recovery is proceeding as expected."
Separately, the Vatican said Leo had received the Vatican chief of staff, or "substitute," Archbishop Paolo Rudelli, and had resumed working from the hospital. Rudelli handles much of the day-to-day administrative work of the Holy See.
For a second day Leo celebrated Mass with other priests in a special chapel set up near his room on the 10th floor of the hospital, spokesman Matteo Bruni said.
The 71-year-old Leo had the lower right lobe of his right lung removed on Tuesday after doctors identified a suspected cancerous nodule. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma , the most common type of lung cancer.
Doctors are still awaiting the results of tests to understand the precise molecular makeup of the cancer, whether it has spread beyond the lobe and whether any further treatment is necessary.
Asked if any changes to Leo's planned trip to South America from Nov. 6-17 were expected, Bruni pointed to Leo's words on Sunday when he announced the discovery of the nodule and impending surgery.
"Thank you for your prayers for the pastoral visit I will make to Peru," Leo said Sunday in Spanish, in a greeting delivered to a Peruvian group. The trip is also scheduled to include stops in Uruguay and Argentina.
Leo is expected to remain hospitalized until at least Oct. 20.

A Dragon has settled into its nest after a more than two-day-long orbital pursuit.
SpaceX's cargo Dragon , flying the CRS-35 (35th Commercial Resupply Services) mission for NASA , rendezvoused with the International Space Station (ISS) this morning (Oct. 15), delivering fresh food, long-term provisions, research and hardware to the orbital lab and its crew.
Coverage of Dragon's arrival at the ISS began at 9:00 a.m. EDT (1315 GMT), as the spacecraft approached from approximately 2.3 miles (3.6 km) away. NASA astronaut Anil Menon served as the station's prime crew member this morning, responsible for monitoring Dragon's approach and autonomous procedures. Docking occurred with the space-face port of the station's Harmony module at 10:27 a.m. EDT (1427 GMT), as the ISS flew about 250 miles (400 km) above South Africa, traveling around 17,500 mph (28,000 kph).
Dragon's arrival brings more than 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of food, research equipment and other supplies, including flight support equipment to replace components on the Canadarm2, a toilet dose pump, a toilet pretreat quality sensor, a robot micro-conical tool used for station maintenance and the very last of eight upgraded solar panels designed to augment the station's power capabilities.
In addition to the usual provisions carried on this mission, Dragon also brought a special suprise for Menon, who is celebrating his 50th birthday today, according to NASA's broadcast spokesperson.
CRS-35 launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the company's pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Tuesday (Oct. 13). Liftoff occurred at 6:35 a.m. EDT (1035 GMT), and the Falcon 9's upper stage deployed the Dragon in low Earth orbit (LEO) a short 10 minutes later. Thanks to the trajectory of the space station's orbit and the near-dawn hour of the launch, the Falcon 9's ascent to orbit was viewed by millions up and down the U.S. East Coast , who witnessed a rare "space jellyfish" phenomenon from the rocket's exhaust plume.
The supplies delivered on CRS-35 will largely support the station's newest astronaut inhabitants, the members of SpaceX's Crew-13 mission for NASA. The four-person crew arrived aboard the ISS on Oct. 1, relieving the members of Crew-12, who returned to Earth a week later.
Crew-12 astronauts will address the media this afternoon (Oct. 15) to discuss their mission and their return after nearly eight months on orbit. A live broadcast of that event will also be available to stream on Space.com's homepage beginning at 3:30 p.m. EDT (1930 GMT).
Cargo Dragon's nominal orbital insertion on Tuesday placed it on course to catch up with the ISS after a 51-hour LEO chase. After rendezvous this morning, Dragon will autonomously dock to the zenith port on the station's Harmony module. It will remain docked with the ISS for about a month before being packed with supplies, waste and research for its return, safe splashdown and recovery on Earth.
Josh Dinner is Space.com's Spaceflight Staff Writer and a photographer with a passion for science and space exploration. He has worked the space beat since 2016, covering the evolution of NASA's commercial spaceflight partnerships and crewed missions from the Space Coast, planetary science missions, the Artemis program and humanity's return to the moon and more. He also enjoys building 1:144-scale model rockets and spacecraft. Find some of Josh's launch photography on Instagram , and follow him on X , where he mostly posts in haiku.

articles.title_zh: Microsoft’s new Photos app combines your PC, OneDrive, and iCloud galleries
articles.content_orig:
Photos for Windows 11 has a redesigned image editor and viewer.
Photos for Windows 11 has a redesigned image editor and viewer.
Microsoft has redesigned its Photos app for Windows 11, overhauling the editor and image viewer, and combining photos and videos from your PC, OneDrive, and iCloud into a single space. The new combined gallery experience aims to make it easier to manage and view your photos without jumping between apps or devices, while also improving app launch and scrolling performance in Photos.
To combine your galleries in the Windows 11 Photos app, you’ll need to turn on Camera Backup in the OneDrive mobile app on iOS or Android, and follow Apple’s guide to set up iCloud for Windows. Once combined in the Windows 11 Photos app, you can browse by date, organize and share albums, search for specific photos via descriptions or by the people featured in them, and more. You can browse files online or offline, and Microsoft says photos will be available on your device “even when you’re not connected.”
The new Photos editor has been “rebuilt from the ground up,” according to Microsoft, launching 25 percent faster and arranging tools into four categories: Crop, Enhance, Repair, and Stylize. The Photos app now also preserves HDR quality during editing processes and allows you to edit and save HEIC and WebP images without altering their original format.
Lastly, the viewer has been given a cleaner layout and performance enhancements, launching 15 percent faster and opening HEIC images up to 30 percent faster, according to Microsoft’s announcement. Media type support has also expanded to SVG files. These new Photos experiences are rolling out today as an update for Windows Insiders on Windows 11, with Microsoft expecting a full launch for all Windows 11 users later this year.

Newswise — Hackensack Meridian (HMH) JFK Johnson Rehabilitation Institute is proud to announce it has received official accreditation from (CARF) Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities International for its Disorders of Consciousness (DoC) Specialty Program. This historic milestone makes HMH JFK Johnson Rehabilitation Institute the first accredited DoC program in the United States and the world.
The prestigious DoC Specialty Designation was awarded to both the facility’s Acute Inpatient Rehabilitation Program and its skilled nursing Extended Recovery Unit. Having partnered with CARF International as an accredited rehabilitation program since 1972, JFK Johnson Rehabilitation Institute is being commended for its unwavering commitment to enhancing the lives of individuals with disorders of consciousness and supporting their families through complex medical journeys.
“HMH JFK Johnson Rehabilitation Institute should be commended on receiving the first Disorders of Consciousness Specialty Designation in the world in both their Acute Inpatient Rehabilitation Program and their skilled nursing Extended Recovery Unit. Their commitment to enhancing the lives of individuals with Disorders of Consciousness and their family/support systems is admirable,” said Terrence Carolan, MSPT, MBA, Managing Director, Medical Rehabilitation and Aging Services, CARF International.
“Being the first program in the world to achieve this specialized CARF accreditation is a testament to the unparalleled dedication and expertise of our entire clinical team,” said Dr. Sara Cuccurullo , chair, vice president, medical director, HMH JFK Johnson Rehabilitation Institute. “For decades, we have been committed to pushing the boundaries of brain injury rehabilitation. This designation validates our transdisciplinary approach and, most importantly, ensures that our patients and their families receive the most advanced, compassionate, and specialized care available when they need it most.”
“Achieving this first-of-its-kind designation from CARF International reflects our continuous investment in providing world-class rehabilitation services,” said Anthony Cuzzola, vice president, Rehabilitation Service Line, Hackensack Meridian Health. “We are immensely proud of our outstanding team. This milestone reinforces our mission to ensure that patients and families facing the most challenging brain injuries have access to an optimal environment designed to maximize their potential for recovery.”
Historically, access to inpatient rehabilitation for individuals recovering from moderate and severe brain injuries has been heavily limited. The new CARF accreditation standards address this critical gap by driving a person and family-centered approach, ensuring that individuals with DoC have better access to timely, specialized, and life-changing rehabilitation.
As the world’s first CARF-accredited DoC Specialty Program, HMH JFK Johnson Rehabilitation Institute demonstrates the profound commitment, specialized capabilities, and resources required to address the complex needs of this patient population. articles.title_orig: Pope Leo resumes working, sees top aide in hospital as doctors say lung recovered from surgery
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo resumes working, sees top aide in hospital as doctors say lung recovered from surgery
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV is recovering well after surgery for lung cancer, as a Southeast Texas doctor says early detection can make a significant difference in treatment outcomes.
The Vatican says doctors removed part of the pope's right lung, and recent tests show he is healing well. Questions remain about whether he will be able to travel to South America as planned.
Dr. Ernest Hymel with Baptist Hospitals of Southeast Texas says lung cancer can be highly treatable when caught early, with cure rates reaching 90% in some cases.
But early-stage lung cancer often causes no symptoms, making screening an important tool for detecting the disease before it advances.
"Most lung cancers don't have any symptoms when they're very early, which can be a little scary," Hymel said. "But that, you know, leads us to the importance of doing screening."
As the disease progresses, symptoms may become more noticeable.
"More advanced lung cancers, obviously, you can have some shortness of breath or coughing. Sometimes even coughing up blood," Hymel said.
Hymel also said advances in radiation therapy and immunotherapy are expanding treatment options for people with lung cancer.
The pope's recovery and future travel plans remain under observation as he continues healing from surgery.

articles.title_zh: Multiple states report suspicious packages with white powder at election offices
articles.content_orig:
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) walks through the U.S. Capitol Building on September 17. Credit: Getty Images/Andrew Harnik
WASHINGTON — New York Sen. Chuck Schumer’s Washington D.C. office was among intended targets of mysterious envelopes, at least some containing a white substance, that had been sent to lawmakers and election officials nationwide , the Democratic leader's spokesman James Martin confirmed to Newsday. A law enforcement official, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss an ongoing investigation, told Newsday that known samples of the powder tested so far have been determined to be "not hazardous," and not a threat. Envelopes were sent to elected officials in U.S. Senate offices, and well as some state and local officials, nationally.
In a statement, an FBI spokesman said, "We are also working with our partners to identify the individual or individuals responsible for the letters. This FBI will continue to safeguard the public and secure elections for American citizens."
Martin said the package never reached the office.
"The envelope was intercepted" by security protocols, Martin said the office was informed.
It was not immediately clear if some of the other envelopes, reached their destinations. A spokeswoman for New York’s junior senator, Kirsten Gillibrand, would not say if her office had been targeted. The office of Long Island Rep. Andrew Garbarino (R-Bayport), the chairman of the House Committee on Homeland Security, said it was not targeted with a package that was intercepted. Lawmakers from both chambers were sent notices by their respective chambers’ sergeant-at-arms to keep an eye out for additional letters.

articles.title_orig: Samsung says the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is more popular than ever thanks to iPhone Duo
articles.title_zh: Samsung says the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is more popular than ever thanks to iPhone Duo
articles.content_orig:
Apple’s debut in the foldable market was always going to have an impact on Android foldables, with many brands having been optimistic that it would have a positive ripple effect. For Samsung, that appears to be true, as the company says that interest in its Galaxy Z Fold 8 remains significantly higher following the iPhone Duo’s announcement.
Speaking to Forbes , Samsung’s UK VP over mobile said that demand for Galaxy Z Fold 8 has risen following the debut of iPhone Duo, with search interest even higher — apparently up by 300%.
Samsung’s foldable momentum is undeniable… Customer demand for the Galaxy Z Fold8 family has increased 16% since launch, and with a 300% increase in active Google searches for Samsung foldables in the last month alone, our market leadership is stronger than ever.
It’s not hard to imagine why this might be the case.
Apple’s massive and loyal fanbase means that the launch of iPhone Duo put foldables under the spotlight for effectively the first time for a lot of potential buyers, so it only makes sense that at least a portion of those users are curious to see what else is out there. Samsung’s lower prices and more refined design might also have a few folks interested enough to give the alternative a shot.
Galaxy Z Fold 8 is currently available for $1,699 on Amazon , $300 less than iPhone Duo, while Samsung.com is offering the Fold 8 for even less than that, with a special discount on the 1TB trim that offers the device for just $50 more than Apple’s base 256GB model.

articles.title_orig: Justice Score GTA VI , Share Tame Impala/SZA/King Gizzard Collab “Flower In A Hurricane”
articles.title_zh: Justice Score GTA VI , Share Tame Impala/SZA/King Gizzard Collab “Flower In A Hurricane”
articles.content_orig:
10:22 AM EDT on October 15, 2026
We are just a little more than a month away from the release of Grand Theft Auto VI , which promises to be the fall's defining cultural event. The new game's blockbuster reach extends in all directions, including music. There's going to be a 34-song soundtrack album with contributions from a baffling array of big stars, and we've already heard a deep selection of its tracks. GTA VI will have more big stars hosting its in-game radio stations . And the game will have a score from French blog-house titans Justice, whose trashy-thrills retro sensibility seems perfect for Vice City shenanigans.
Today, Rockstar Games unveils its GTA VI launch trailer and unveils Justice as the composers of the game's score. Those two things are related to each other because the trailer is scored by a brand-new Justice track with a bunch of superstar collaborators. On "Flower In A Hurricane," Justice team up with Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard — a whole lot of people for one song.
The track itself is an '80s-style synth-rock anthem with a dramatic opening-riff moment that reminds me of Dire Straits' "Money For Nothing." Justice previously teamed up with Tame Impala for "One Night/All Night" and the Grammy-winning " Neverender ," from their last album, 2024's Hyperdrama . A decade ago, Tame Impala's Kevin Parker and SZA also worked on some tracks with Mark Ronson, but they were never released.
For most of "Flower In A Hurricane," Parker and SZA sing together in harmony. It's not clear what Parker's fellow Australian psych wizards in King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard did to the track, but I'm sure some of the triumphant organ and guitar action comes from them. As for the trailer, it just looks fucking awesome. I am about to waste so much of my life on this game. I'm not saying that for any kind of advertising purpose. I'm just saying they got me.
Other excerpts from Justice's GTA VI score apparently already appeared in Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look , a half-hour game preview that you can watch on Netflix. There may or may not be some kind of game-score release, but "Flower In A Hurricane" will be one of the 34 tracks on GTA VI: The Album . Below, check out that song and the new trailer.
Grand Theft Auto VI and its accompanying album are both out 11/19.

articles.title_orig: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs reportedly injured in prison fight with Jamaican drug lord
articles.title_zh: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs reportedly injured in prison fight with Jamaican drug lord
articles.content_orig:
Ninfa Saavedra , Digital Content Specialist
Sean “Diddy” Combs reportedly suffered a head injury during a fight with fellow inmate Christopher “Dudus” Coke at a federal prison in New Jersey, according to a report from TMZ .
The alleged altercation happened Friday, Oct. 9, at the Federal Correctional Institution Fort Dix, TMZ reported, citing multiple sources inside the prison.
According to TMZ, the fight stemmed from frustration among inmates following reports about Combs’ alleged treatment behind bars. The outlet reported that inmates were upset after an NBC News report detailed claims that Combs had access to special privileges and contraband while incarcerated.
TMZ reported that prison officials conducted at least two raids following the reports and confiscated cellphones from inmates, including Coke. Sources told the outlet that some inmates blamed Combs for the increased scrutiny.
Coke, also known as “Dudus,” is a Jamaican drug lord who has been serving a 23-year federal prison sentence since 2012, according to published reports.
The alleged fight came shortly before Combs was transported from the prison by ambulance early Saturday, Oct. 10, after suffering a head injury.
Combs was taken outside the prison for medical treatment and returned to the facility before sunrise. A source familiar with the situation told PEOPLE that the injury was not life-threatening and that Combs returned to prison the same day.
Combs’ spokesperson, Juda Engelmayer, told PEOPLE that his health and well-being were the immediate concern and thanked those who had reached out.
The circumstances surrounding the injury were initially unclear. TMZ later reported that the injury occurred during the alleged fight with Coke.
Combs is serving a 50-month federal prison sentence after being convicted in 2025 on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. He was acquitted of more serious sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy charges.
He is currently incarcerated at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey. Federal prison records list his projected release date as March 2, 2028.
The alleged altercation and the details surrounding it have not been independently confirmed by prison officials.
